INT_ITERATOR_TO_INT and LONG_ITERATOR_TO_LONG return the current value of an IntIterator/LongIterator without advancing it. MAX_PROPERTY_LENGTH is 250.

applyPermissions(rules, user, stack, resolver, pass) starts at pass and replaces the level by each rule's apply(user, level, stack, resolver) in order, returning the final level; a null rule list returns pass.

getSingleParameterLong(map, name) and getSingleLong(value) take the first element of a collection, Object[] or long[] (empty gives null); a Number gives its longValue(); a non-blank String is parsed as a long, falling back to double parsing truncated toward zero ("2.9" gives 2, "1e3" gives 1000); anything else, blank text or a missing key gives null; unparsable text logs a warning and gives null. A null map or name gives null.
getSingleParameterInteger reads like getSingleParameterLong but returns an Integer and gives null (with a warning) when the value is outside the int range.

getSingleParameterBoolean returns a Boolean value as is; otherwise it is true only when the single string value equals true ignoring case after trimming; missing values, a null map or a null name give false.

getSingleString(value) returns String.valueOf of the first element of a collection or String[] (null if empty), String.valueOf of any other non-null value (other arrays are not unwrapped), and null for null. getSingleParameter(map, name) is getSingleString of the map value, null for a null map or name.

getStringList(value) returns for a collection a new list of String.valueOf of its non-null elements; for a String[] a fixed-size list backed by the array (immutable empty if the array is empty); for null an immutable empty list; for anything else a one-element list of its text. getMultiParameter(map, name) applies it to the map value (empty list for null map or name). getMultiParameterLong parses each string with STRING_LONG into a new list, keeping null entries for unparsable strings.

getCommaSeparatedParameter(map, name, converter) splits the single string parameter at commas with String.split semantics (parts not trimmed, trailing empty parts dropped, e.g. a,,b, gives a, empty, b) and converts each part, returning a new list; a null or blank parameter gives an empty list.

setLongProperty(props, name, value) stores value (null as empty) in chunks of at most 250 chars under name, name.1, name.2, ... and then sets to null the following numbered entries while they hold non-empty values. getLongProperty(props, name) concatenates name, name.1, ... until the first missing or empty entry, returning an empty string if nothing is stored.
getBooleanSystemProperty(key, default) returns true only when the system property is set to true (any case), false for any other set value, and default when it is not set or the key is null or empty.
lastOrZero(list) returns the last element or 0 for null or empty. listsEqual(a, b) is true when both are null or empty, false when exactly one is, else element-wise equality.
copyPermissions(rules) returns a new list of clones of every rule in order (empty for null); copyPermissionsOrNull returns null for null and otherwise the same.

appendDebugIssueString(id, key, sb) appends (KEY ID), e.g. (ABC-1 10000), when the key is non-null and just the ID otherwise. getDebugIssueString(Issue) returns null text for null, else that label from the issue's key and ID. getDebugIssueString(Long) and appendDebugIssueString(Long, sb) give null text for null and otherwise look the key up via getDebugIssueKey, which returns null on any failure.
issueKeyOrId(issue, id) returns the issue's key when the issue is non-null, else "issue #<id>" when the ID is non-null, else "(no issue ID)".

appendDebugStructureString(id, manager, sb) appends the structure name in single quotes followed by " (#<id>)", e.g. 'Plan' (#12), reading the structure with security checks suspended; if loading throws StructureException it appends #<id>. getDebugStructureString returns the same text.

username(user) gives anonymous for null, the user's name, or user[name = null] if the name is null. debugConstant(c) and debugAction(a) give <null> for null and otherwise name(id), e.g. Bug(1). getDebugRowString(long) gives (row N); getDebugRowString(StructureRow) gives the row's toString() or the empty string for null.

getTextInCurrentUserLocale(key, params) returns JiraI18n.forCurrentUser().getText(key, params); the I18nText form uses its key and arguments (NullPointerException for null). getText(locale, user, key, params) uses JiraI18n.create(locale, user). getJiraDefaultLocale() returns Jira's default locale, or Locale.ROOT with a logged warning when it is not available.

getUserKey and getUserName return the user's key/login name or null for null; getGroupName returns the group name or null. getUserByKey resolves a key through JiraFunc.USERKEY_APPLICATIONUSER; getUserNameByKey returns that user's name or null; getApplicationUserByName asks Jira's user manager. migrateUserNameToUserKey lower-cases the name with Crowd's identifier rules (null gives null).
createRuntimeSignature() returns an int derived from the current time, the nanosecond timer and an identity hash code, varying between calls and JVM runs.

toJson(obj) serializes with a Jackson mapper omitting null properties and returns the empty string for null or on failure. fromJson(text, cls) and fromJson(text) return null for null or empty text and on parse failure (fromJson(text) also for non-object JSON). toMap(obj) converts a bean to a Map via Jackson (null properties omitted) and returns null on failure. toDebugJson(obj) returns the empty string for null, a String unchanged, otherwise JSON including null properties, or ?<error>? on failure.
onlyOneIsTrue(booleans...) is true exactly when one argument is true; false for none, for no arguments and for two or more.
swap(list, a, b) exchanges the elements at positions a and b in place; invalid positions throw IndexOutOfBoundsException.

getItemDisplayable(itemIds, service) loads the displayable text and URL attributes for all items in one request and returns a new map from each identity to an ItemDisplayable, using the identity's toString() when the text is missing or empty. The single-identity and StructureRow forms return the ItemDisplayable for that item (never null). getItemDescription(itemId) obtains the attribute service itself and returns the description, or null on any failure or when the service is unavailable.

StructureUtil's nn, nnv, lv, iv, lvn, ivn, nnl, nni, setType, mapType and listType behave exactly as the TypeUtils methods of the same names; isMutuallyExclusive as IntegersUtil's; isSubMap as MapUtils'; warnExceptionIfDebug and getMessageWithCauseChain as LoggingUtils'.
getBaseUrl() returns the base URL from the SAL application-properties service, the empty string if it reports null, and the empty string with a warning if the service is unavailable.

encodeURL encodes UTF-8 form-style (space as +, unreserved .-*_ kept, others %XX upper-case) and decodeURL decodes it; both return the empty string for null and decodeURL returns malformed input unchanged. encodeURIComponent writes spaces as %20 and leaves ! ' ( ) ~ unescaped, e.g. a b(c) gives a%20b(c).
isDevMode() is true when system property jira.dev.mode or atlassian.dev.mode equals exactly true (case-sensitive).
nonBlank(s) returns s trimmed; null, empty or whitespace-only input throws IllegalArgumentException with message "argument cannot be null or blank".

memoize(supplier) returns a non-thread-safe Supplier that calls the original only on the first get() and returns that same result (null included) afterwards; a supplier already returned by memoize is returned as is. If the first call throws, later calls return null without retrying (as the original does).

ToString.begin(name) returns a new StringBuilder with name followed by {; each append(sb, name, value) appends name=value, (for int, long, boolean and Object via String.valueOf) and returns the same builder; end(sb) removes one trailing comma (when the builder is longer than one char), appends } and returns the text. begin("Foo"), a=1, b=x, end gives Foo{a=1,b=x}; with no fields Foo{}. The String constants BEGIN, EQ, SEP and END hold the texts "{", "=", "," and "}".

TotalOrder.wrap turns Long, Integer, Short and Byte values into ComparableTuple.of(long) and Double and Float into ComparableTuple.of(double), so numbers of different classes compare numerically (compare(1, 1.0) == 0 and compare(2L, 1.5f) > 0); other non-string objects are kept as is; null stays null.

withStrictStringComparison compares strings with String.compareTo; withCaseInsensitiveStringComparison(locale) lower-cases strings with the locale (root for null or the no-arg form), so "ABC" and "abc" compare equal; withCollatorStringComparison(locale[, strength[, decomposition]]) and withCollator(collator) compare with a java.text.Collator (withCollator(null) behaves strictly).

COMPARATOR orders wrappers: null values last (two nulls equal); same runtime class by compareTo when Comparable, else by toString(); different classes put numbers (ComparableTuple) first, then String, then other classes by simple class name. So compare(5, "a") < 0, compare("a", null) < 0, and compare(Boolean.TRUE, new java.util.Date()) < 0 (Boolean before Date by name).

TotalOrder.ValueWrapper getValue returns the normalized value, getValueClass its class (null for null), isComparable whether it is Comparable, getOrder the producing order, toString String.valueOf of the value (e.g. (5) for 5). wrap(value, payload) returns a TotalOrder.PayloadWrapper whose getPayload is the payload and whose toString is the value text followed by the payload in parentheses, e.g. (5)(x).
setType(), mapType() and listType() return java.util.Set.class, java.util.Map.class and java.util.List.class.
nn(Long, long) and nn(Integer, int) return the value or the default for null; nnv(v, d) returns v or d for null; nn(String) returns "" for null; nnl and nni return 0 for null.
lv(s, d) and iv(s, d) parse a decimal long/int without trimming and return d for null or invalid text (" 5", "1.5", overflow); lvn and ivn return null instead.
fitsIntoInt(v) is true when v is within -2147483648..2147483647.

Once the plugin has stopped the component, every `StructureManager` lookup, permission, create, copy and delete method throws the unchecked `StructureStoppedException`; so does `saveChanges()` on a structure obtained earlier (after its blank-name check). Before the component has been started the methods work normally. `addListener` and `removeListener` never throw for this reason.

On start the component registers a scheduled job with the `ScheduledJobManager` under the key `forestChanges.lastCleanTime` and adds a statistics source; on stop it removes that job and stops receiving history batches, so registered `StructureListener`s are no longer called for later batches.

The statistics source added on start reports four values computed over all stored structures: `structureCount` (all structures, archived included), `editRequiresParentPermCount` (structures with the edit-requires-parent-issue-permission flag, not counting the structure with ID 1), `archivedCount`, and `structuresWithApplyRule` (structures with at least one `PermissionRule.ApplyStructure` rule). It is collected locally only (SPEC.md 1.8).

`getStructure(id, level)` throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the ID is null, when no row with that ID exists in `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE` (this includes IDs that are zero, negative or outside the 32-bit int range), and when the current user's level on an existing structure does not include `level`. A null `level` accepts any existing structure, even one on which the user's level is `NONE` (as long as it exists). When security is overridden (`StructureAuth`) no level is checked.

Each `getStructure` call (and each element of every list returned by the manager) is a new, independent `Structure` object holding a snapshot of the stored values: setters on one object are not seen by another object for the same ID, and a stored change becomes visible only in objects obtained after `saveChanges()` returned.
`getStructure` returns archived structures as well; `isArchived()` on the result reflects `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE.C_ARCHIVED`.

A structure read from the store reports: `getName()` from `C_NAME`; `getDescription()` from `C_DESCRIPTION` (empty string when NULL); `getOwnerUserKey()` from `C_OWNER` (null when NULL); `getPermissions()` and `isEditRequiresParentIssuePermission()` decoded from `C_PERMISSONS` as described in SPEC.md 1.5, with the stored level `EDIT_GENERATORS` returned as `PermissionLevel.AUTOMATE`; a NULL `C_PERMISSONS` gives an empty rule list and flag false.

`getAllStructures`, `getArchivedStructures`, `getStructuresOwnedBy`, `getStructuresByName` and `hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser` first ask `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToUser` for the current user (null when anonymous); when it answers false they return an empty list (false) without reading structures. When security is overridden this question is not asked and no per-structure permission filter is applied, so all stored structures matching the other criteria are returned.

In the listing methods each structure is kept only when the current user's permission level on it (as `getStructurePermission(id, user)` computes it) includes the requested level; a null requested level keeps every structure, including those where the level is `NONE`, provided the plugin is available to the user.

Lists from `getAllStructures`, `getArchivedStructures`, `getStructuresOwnedBy` and `getStructuresByName` are new lists sorted ascending by `java.text.Collator` collation keys of the structure names, using the collator `StructurePluginHelper.getCollator` returns for the current user. The order of structures whose names collate equal is not defined.

`getAllStructures(level)` and `getAllStructures(level, false)` leave out archived structures; `getAllStructures(level, true)` includes them; `getArchivedStructures(level)` returns only archived structures. All three apply the same availability and level rules.

`getStructuresOwnedBy(user)` returns the non-archived structures whose stored owner key equals `user.getKey()` and on which the current user has at least `VIEW` (no level check when security is overridden). A null user returns an empty list, since stored owners always have a key. Structures without an owner are never returned.

`getStructuresByName(name, level, searchArchived)` returns an empty list for a null name or one that is empty after trimming. Otherwise it compares the trimmed argument with each stored name trimmed, using `String.equalsIgnoreCase`, so " Plan " finds "plan"; archived structures are only considered when `searchArchived` is true; the two-argument form uses false. Availability and level filtering and sorting are as for the other listings.

`hasNonArchivedStructuresForUser()` is true when at least one non-archived structure exists on which the current user has `VIEW` (any non-archived structure when security is overridden), and false when the plugin is not available to the user.

`getSingleViewableStructureId()` returns null when `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser()` is false (this is checked even when security is overridden). Otherwise it returns the ID of the only non-archived structure the current user can view, or null when there are none or several. The answer is cached per user key (anonymous shares one entry) for up to 5 minutes, and is dropped earlier whenever a structure is created, saved or deleted.

`isIssueInStructureNoAccessCheck(issueId, structureId)` returns false when either argument is null, zero or negative. Otherwise it is true exactly when `AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX` has a row for that issue and structure with `C_OCCURRENCES` > 0 (answers are cached per issue). No permission or archived check is made, and only the stored forest counts.

`getViewableStructuresWithIssue(issueId)` returns an empty list for a null issue ID. Otherwise it takes the structures listed in `AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX` for the issue with a positive count, drops those that no longer exist or are archived, keeps those on which the current user has `VIEW` (all of them when security is overridden), and sorts the result with `StructurePluginHelper.getStructureComparator(current user)`. It does not call the plugin-availability check itself; a user without access gets level `NONE` and so an empty list unless a Jira administrator.

Each forest change of a stored structure adjusts `AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX` by the net number of issue rows added and removed per issue (a row is created when missing, updated, or deleted when its count reaches 0; duplicate rows for one pair are deleted, keeping the first). The update runs as a one-shot background job; when the job cannot be scheduled it runs synchronously. So `isIssueInStructureNoAccessCheck` and `getViewableStructuresWithIssue` may lag briefly behind a forest change. Rows for issues under generators are never written, since only stored rows are counted.

`getStructurePermission(id)` and `getStructurePermission(id, user)` return `PermissionLevel.NONE` when the ID is null or no such structure exists; they never throw for a missing structure. Neither takes security override into account; the one-argument form uses `StructureAuth.getUser()`.

A user who holds Jira's global `ADMINISTER` permission (asked through `GlobalPermissionManager`; never true for anonymous) gets `ADMIN` on every existing structure, even when the plugin is not available to that user and regardless of rules and owner. This can be turned off with the dark feature `structure.permissions.jiraAdminHasAllPermissions` set to false (read once at start).

For a user who is not a Jira administrator and to whom the plugin is not available (`StructureConfiguration.isStructureAvailable(user)` false), the level on every structure is `NONE`, whatever the rules say.
The owner of a structure (stored owner key equal to the user's key) gets `ADMIN` on it; the structure's rules are not consulted then. An anonymous caller is never the owner.

For other users the level starts at `NONE` and the structure's rules are applied in list order: a `PermissionRule.SetLevel` whose subject matches the user replaces the current level with the rule's level (a later matching rule overrides an earlier one, including lowering it); a non-matching rule leaves it. A `PermissionRule.ApplyStructure` applies the rules (not the owner) of the referenced structure at that point, recursively, continuing from the current level; a reference to a missing structure, to the structure itself or one that closes a cycle is skipped. A null rule is skipped; a null resulting level is reported as `NONE`.

Subject matching when computing levels: `Anyone` matches every user including anonymous; `JiraUser` matches the user with the same key; `JiraGroup` asks Jira's `GroupManager.isUserInGroup(user, groupName)`; `ProjectRole` matches only when both its project ID and role ID are non-zero, the project and role exist in Jira (`ProjectManager`, `ProjectRoleManager`), and `ProjectRoleManager.isUserInProjectRole` is true.

Computed levels are cached per structure ID and user key for up to 5 minutes. The whole permission cache (levels, app-permission answers, the single-viewable-structure answer) is cleared, on every cluster node, when a structure is created, saved or deleted; changes outside the plugin (Jira group membership, project roles, Jira administrator rights, plugin availability) may take up to 5 minutes to affect the computed levels.

`isAccessible(id, level)` is false for a null ID or a structure that does not exist, also when security is overridden; for an existing structure it is true when security is overridden, otherwise it is true when the current user's level includes `level` (a null level is always included).

`isGeneratorConfigurationAllowed(id, user)` and `isEffectorConfigurationAllowed(id, user)` are true only when the given user's level on the structure (as `getStructurePermission(id, user)`) includes `AUTOMATE` and `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed` grants that user `CoreAppPermissions.CONFIGURE_GENERATORS` (respectively `CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS`). `isEffectorExecutionAllowed(id, user)` needs at least `VIEW` and `CoreAppPermissions.EXECUTE_EFFECTORS`. All three are false for a null or missing structure ID, ignore security override, and treat a null user as anonymous.

`createStructure()` returns a new structure with ID 0, empty name and description, no owner, no rules, both flags false; it writes nothing and makes no permission check. Nothing about it is visible to other calls until `saveChanges()`.

`saveChanges()` on a new structure (after the blank-name check), unless security is overridden: throws `StructureException` with `NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE` when `StructurePluginHelper.isCreateStructureAllowed(current user)` is false; then validates its permission rules (see the rule-validation claims) and, when an owner is set, the owner (see the owner claim). Nothing is stored when a check fails.

Saving a new structure inserts one `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE` row (C_NAME, C_DESCRIPTION with empty stored as NULL, C_OWNER, C_ARCHIVED, C_PERMISSONS encoded as in SPEC.md 1.5 with `AUTOMATE` written as `EDIT_GENERATORS`, NULL when there are no rules and the flag is off) and gives the structure its generated ID (`getId()` then returns it). It then removes any leftover `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST` and `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE` rows, history and issue index rows for that ID, and inserts an `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST` row with the empty forest and version 0. The new structure appears in listings immediately.

When a new structure is saved without an owner, the current user (`StructureAuth.getUser()`) becomes its owner; when there is no current user (anonymous, e.g. under security override with no user) it is stored with no owner (C_OWNER NULL).

`saveChanges()` on an existing structure whose values differ from the values it was loaded with, unless security is overridden: throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the current user's level is `NONE`, and with `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` when it is below `ADMIN` (so renaming, describing, archiving or un-archiving all need `ADMIN`). When the rule list changed it validates the new rules for that structure; when the owner changed it validates the owner. If the row was deleted meanwhile it throws `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`.

Updating an existing structure writes only the `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE` columns whose values changed: C_NAME, C_DESCRIPTION (empty as NULL), C_OWNER (NULL for no owner), C_ARCHIVED, and C_PERMISSONS when either the rules or the edit-requires-parent-issue-permission flag changed.

`saveChanges()` writes nothing and checks no permission when no setter was called on the object since it was obtained or last saved, or when setters were called but every value ends up equal to the loaded one (for example `setName` with the same name): it then succeeds even for a user without `ADMIN` (as the original does). In the second case (a setter was called) caches are still refreshed and the item-changed notification below is still sent.

After a successful insert or update, `saveChanges()` clears the permission caches on all nodes, makes the new values visible to later `getStructure` and listing calls, records an item change for `CoreIdentities.structure(id)` with the `ItemTracker`, and returns the same instance, which can be modified and saved again.

Owner validation (only when security is not overridden): a Jira administrator (`StructurePluginHelper.isAdmin`) may set any owner. On an existing structure a user who holds Jira's `USER_PICKER` global permission and has `ADMIN` on the structure (or is its previous owner) may also set any owner, including none. In every other case the only allowed new owner is the current user; anything else (another user, or no owner) throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_OWNER_EDIT_DENIED`. For a new structure this means a non-administrator can only name himself as owner.

Rule validation on save (only when security is not overridden), in list order, first failure wins: a `SetLevel` with a null subject throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_PARAMETER`; a `JiraUser` subject fails with error code 6013 (category NOT_FOUND) when the current user lacks Jira's `USER_PICKER` global permission or the user key does not resolve to a Jira user; a `JiraGroup` fails with code 6010 when the group is not in `StructurePluginHelper.getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser()`; a `ProjectRole` with project ID 0 fails with `INVALID_PARAMETER`, one whose project is not in `getStructureProjectsForCurrentUser()` with code 6011, one whose role is not in `getAvailableRoles()` with code 6012. `Anyone` always passes; the level is not checked; null list entries are ignored.

Rule validation of `ApplyStructure` rules on save: a rule referring to the structure being saved fails with error code 6006 (category INVALID_INPUT); a rule whose structure ID is null, does not exist or on which the current user lacks `ADMIN` fails with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; a rule that would make the chain of applied structures (followed through their own apply rules regardless of the user's access) loop back to a structure already on the path fails with code 6006.

`copyStructureWithoutForest(id, newOwner, copyPermissions)`, unless security is overridden, first throws `StructureException` with `NOT_ALLOWED_TO_CREATE_STRUCTURE` when the current user may not create structures (`StructurePluginHelper.isCreateStructureAllowed`), even if the source does not exist; then throws `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the source is missing, the ID null, or the user lacks `VIEW` on it; then, when `copyPermissions` is true, throws `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` when the user lacks `ADMIN` on the source. Under security override only the existence check remains.

The unsaved copy has ID 0, the source's description, archived false, and as owner `newOwner` when non-null, else the source owner resolved to a Jira user (no owner when that user no longer exists). With `copyPermissions` true it gets a copy of the source's rules and its edit-requires-parent-issue-permission flag; with false it has no rules and the flag off. Its name is the localized text for key `s.structure.copyof` with arguments (source name, the current `java.util.Date`); the English text is `Copy of <name> (<short date> <short time>)`. The source is not changed and nothing is stored.

Because saving a new structure only lets a non-administrator name himself as owner, `copyStructure(id, null, …)` by a user who is not a Jira administrator, on a structure owned by someone else, fails with `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_OWNER_EDIT_DENIED` when the copy is saved, and nothing is created (as the original does). Copying with `copyPermissions` true also fails at save when a copied rule does not pass rule validation for the current user (for example a group he is not in).

`copyStructure(id, newOwner, copyPermissions)` performs the same checks, saves the copy (as `saveChanges()` would, with the same permission and owner checks) and then adds the source's current stored forest (its stored rows, generators not run) at the top level of the copy's empty forest, acting as the current user and subject to the same checks and limits as any forest change of that structure. Each copied row gets a new row ID; rows of structure-owned items (generators, effectors, folders) refer to new item copies owned by the new structure. The returned structure is the saved copy. If copying the forest fails, the copy remains stored with an empty forest and the exception is thrown (as the original does).

`deleteStructure(null)` does nothing. For a non-null ID, unless security is overridden, it throws `StructureException` with `STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` (no message) when the current user lacks `ADMIN` on the structure, including when the structure does not exist.

`deleteStructure(id)` deletes, in this order, the `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE` row, the `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST` row, all `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE` rows of the structure, its history, and its `AO_8BAD1B_ISSUE_INDEX` rows, and then publishes a `StructureDeletedEvent` with that ID on the Jira `EventPublisher`. It does not touch generators, synchronizers, favourites or views, and records no item change. Afterwards `getStructure(id, …)` throws `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, and permission caches are cleared.
Under security override, `deleteStructure` of an ID that does not exist succeeds: it deletes nothing and still publishes a `StructureDeletedEvent` for that ID (as the original does).

The replacement does no licence checking (SPEC.md §1.1): creating, saving, copying or deleting structures and changing stored forests never fail, and are never restricted or made read-only, on licence grounds.

`addListener` registers the listener; adding the same instance twice makes it be called twice per batch, and `removeListener` removes one registration (nothing when not registered). Listeners are called synchronously, in registration order, on the thread that finishes the outermost history batch, with a map from structure ID to the `HistoryEntry` recorded for each structure changed in the batch. An exception or `LinkageError` thrown by one listener is logged and the next listeners are still called.

Every `apply` on a stored structure forest opens and closes a history batch, so listeners are called after it even when nothing was recorded (dry run, an action that changes nothing, or a failed action); the map is then empty (as the original does). When the call happens inside an enclosing batch, the call comes only at the end of the outermost batch.

Applying a `ForestAction` to a structure's stored forest (the source `ForestService` returns for `ForestSpec.skeleton(id)`, which reads without checks) still checks the current user, in this order: unless security is overridden, `STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED` when the plugin is not available to the user; `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` when the structure does not exist (also under override) or the user lacks `VIEW`; then, unless overridden, `ARCHIVED_STRUCTURE_EDIT_DENIED` for an archived structure and `STRUCTURE_EDIT_DENIED` when the user lacks `EDIT`. Under security override archived structures can be changed.

A user whose level includes `EDIT` but not `AUTOMATE` (and only when security is not overridden) gets `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_AUTOMATION_EDIT_DENIED` when an add or copy action's fragment contains a generator or effector row, or when a move or remove action touches a row whose subtree contains a generator or effector row. Nothing is changed.

On a structure with edit-requires-parent-issue-permission on (and security not overridden), inserting rows under, or removing or moving rows from under, a parent row fails with `StructureException` `FOREST_CHANGE_PROHIBITED_BY_PARENT_PERMISSIONS` when the parent's item exists but is not visible to the user, or is a Jira issue that `StructurePluginHelper.isIssueEditable(issue, user)` reports as not editable; with `UNAVAILABLE_MODULE` when the parent's item type is not available. Changes at the top level, and parents whose item no longer exists, are not checked.

An add or copy action that would make the stored forest larger than 100000 rows (current size plus fragment size) fails with `StructureException` `FOREST_SOURCE_ACTION_FAILED` and the localized message for `s.error.forest.size-limit-exceeded` with the limit, unless the action parameters set `ignoreSizeLimit` to true. The limit is an internal tuning setting, not part of the contract.

Rows of an added or copied fragment are stored as new persistent rows (new row IDs from the row manager) for the same item and semantics, and `ActionResult.getRowIdReplacements()` maps each fragment row ID that changed to its new ID; it returns an empty map, not null, when nothing was replaced. Items of a structure-owned item type (generators, effectors, folders) are bound to this structure through their item type; for a stored generator this means: a generator owned by no structure is reassigned to this structure, and one already owned by any structure (even this one) is duplicated as a new generator owned by this structure, whose ID the new row refers to. A loop-marker row pointing at a transient row is replaced by that row's item; one pointing at a missing row becomes a folder titled by the i18n key `s.ext.it.folder.missing`. With the parameter `reuseRows` true the fragment's row IDs are kept as they are, unless one of them is already in the forest, in which case new rows are created as usual.

With the action parameter `dryRun` true the checks and the action are carried out on a copy only: nothing is stored, no row is created (fragment rows get temporary negative IDs), no history or forest change row is written and the version stays the same; the result is a success with an empty row ID replacement map.

A successful change rewrites the structure's `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST` row (C_FOREST and C_VERSION) only if the stored version is still the one the change started from; the new version is the old one plus the number of elementary changes, and one `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE` row per elementary change is inserted with versions old+1 … new. An action that leaves the forest unchanged writes nothing and keeps the version. `getLatest()` reflects the change right after `apply` returns.

When the stored version changed concurrently, the change is re-applied to a freshly loaded forest, up to 5 attempts in total with pauses of 0, 100, 200, 400 ms (internal tuning settings, not part of the contract); after the last attempt it throws a `StructureException` with error code 6014 (category INTERNAL) and the message "Could not save changes to structure #<id>: too many concurrent changes to this structure. Please try again later."

Each successful, non-dry-run change records history (one entry per structure per outermost batch, with ADD, COPY, MOVE and REMOVE changes) by the current user, readable through `HistoryService`; changes that are cancelled, dry-run or empty record nothing.

The stored-forest source of a structure that does not exist (or has no `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST` row) returns `VersionedForest.EMPTY` from `getLatest()`; obtaining the source never fails for a missing structure, only `apply` does.

The stored-forest source reports versions as `DataVersion(signature, C_VERSION)` with a signature chosen at random when the source object is created on this node. `getUpdate(from)` returns a full update when `from` has another signature or is newer than the current version, an empty incremental update when it equals the current version, and otherwise an incremental update with the elementary changes from the journal (`AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE`); when the needed changes are no longer in the journal (or locks cannot be obtained in 65 s) it falls back to a full update.

The `forestChanges.lastCleanTime` job runs when at least 12 hours (an internal tuning setting, not part of the contract) have passed since its last run and the plugin is not stopped. For each structure it reads the lowest and highest version in `AO_8BAD1B_FOREST_CHANGE` and deletes the rows with a version below highest − 500 (also tunable internally), so the latest 501 changes stay (one more than the limit, as the original does). Nothing is deleted when the highest equals the lowest.

`getInstalledSynchronizer(null)` returns null without any other work (also while the plugin is stopped). For 0, a negative ID or an ID with no `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row it returns null (logged at info level), never throws.

An instance returned by `getInstalledSynchronizer` reflects its `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row: `getId` is `ID`, `getStructureId` is `C_STRUCTURE_ID`, `getSynchronizerModuleKey` is `C_MODULE_KEY`, `getUserKey` is `C_OWNER`; `getSynchronizer` is the registered `structure-synchronizer` module with that complete key (null when no such module is currently registered), and `getParameters` is that synchronizer's `restoreParameters(C_PARAMETERS)` (null when the synchronizer is null).

When the registered synchronizer's `restoreParameters` throws (any exception or `LinkageError`) for a stored instance, `getInstalledSynchronizer` returns null for that ID and `getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure` leaves the instance out of its list; the failure is logged, not thrown.

Instances are cached per ID (and the ID list per structure) and the caches are invalidated by this module's own install, uninstall, update and autosync changes, so those changes are visible to the next call on the same node. A row written to `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` behind the module's back may not be seen until the cache expires (cache timeout setting `structure.sync.cache.timeout`, slowly expiring) or caches are cleared.

`clearCaches()` (the `CachingComponent` contract) drops the cached instances, per-structure ID lists and the set of autosync-enabled IDs, so the next calls re-read `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE`. `clearUserCaches(user)` does nothing.

`getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure(null)` returns an empty list without other work; 0 gives an empty list. Otherwise it returns one instance per `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row whose `C_STRUCTURE_ID` equals the ID, in the order the database returns them (no sorting), skipping instances that cannot be loaded. When the ID query itself fails it logs and returns an empty list.

`installSynchronizer(sync, structureId, params, user)` throws `StructureSynchronizerException`, checked in this order: synchronizer null (`null synchronizer`), user null (`null user`), `sync.isAvailable()` false (`synchronizer <sync> is not currently available`), structure ID null or not positive (`invalid structure ID <id>`), the synchronizer's complete module key not a currently registered `structure-synchronizer` module (`<descriptor label> (<class name>) is not registered`). The structure's existence and the user's permissions are not checked.

When installing (and in `resyncOnce` and `updateSynchronizer`), the parameters are serialized with the synchronizer's `storeParameters`. A `ClassCastException` becomes a `StructureSynchronizerException` with message `<sync> invalid parameters class`; any other exception or `LinkageError` becomes one with message `<sync> cannot store parameters`; the original is the cause. Nothing is stored in that case.

A successful `installSynchronizer` creates one `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row: `C_STRUCTURE_ID` the structure, `C_MODULE_KEY` the synchronizer's complete module key, `C_OWNER` the user's key, `C_PARAMETERS` the stored parameter text (a blank text, including empty, is stored as null), `C_ENABLED` false. Afterwards `isAutosyncEnabled` of the new ID is false and `getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure` includes it.

The instance returned by `installSynchronizer` has the new auto-generated ID, the structure ID, module key and owner key as stored, `getSynchronizer()` the very synchronizer passed in, and `getParameters()` the same parameter object passed in (not a restored copy).

After installing, the module calls `SyncAuditLog.recordActions(instance, description, null)` with description keys in order `action`=`install`, `loggedInUserKey` (key of the current Structure user, empty string when anonymous), `parameters` (the parameter object passed in, an empty map when null). Since the group has no actions it is only written to the database when empty groups are stored.

The module also offers a restore variant of install (used by backup restore) that takes an explicit instance ID: with a non-zero ID the `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row is created with exactly that `ID`; validation, stored columns, returned instance and the `install` audit record are as for `installSynchronizer`.

`installSynchronizerOffline(moduleKey, parameters, structureId, ownerKey, enabled)` throws `StructureSynchronizerException` `invalid structure ID <id>` when the structure ID is null or not positive, then `null or nonexistent user '<ownerKey>'` when the owner key is blank or Jira's user manager finds no user by that key. The module key is not checked against registered modules (an unknown key is stored as given), but a blank module key makes it throw `IllegalArgumentException` (message `moduleKey = <key>`) before anything is stored.

A successful `installSynchronizerOffline` stores the module key, owner key and parameter text verbatim (blank text as null) with `C_ENABLED` set to the given flag, and returns the new `ID`. When enabled is true, `isAutosyncEnabled` of the new ID is immediately true; no 'autosync enabled' event is recorded for it. It then records an audit group with instance ID, module key and structure ID and description `action`=`installOffline`, `autosyncEnabled` (the flag), `loggedInUserKey`, `parameters` (the parameter string itself, an empty map when null).

`uninstallSynchronizer(id)` deletes that instance's `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row; afterwards `getInstalledSynchronizer(id)` is null, `isAutosyncEnabled(id)` false, and the structure's list no longer contains it. It then records an audit group with the deleted row's instance ID, module key and structure ID and description `action`=`uninstall`, `loggedInUserKey`, `parameters` (the stored parameter string, an empty map when null). Rows in other tables that refer to the instance are not touched.

`uninstallSynchronizer(null)` does nothing (also while stopped). An ID with no row, 0, or one outside the 32-bit range deletes nothing and records no audit group, and does not throw (it only drops the module's caches).

Uninstalling an instance does not cancel a resync of it that was already requested and not yet run: the queued request keeps the owner, structure, module key and parameters captured at request time and still runs on the next sync job pass (as the original does).

`uninstallAllSynchronizers()` deletes every `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row and records one audit group with instance ID 0, module key empty, structure ID 0 and description `action`=`uninstallAll`, `loggedInUserKey` (no `parameters` key).

`uninstallSynchronizersForStructure(null)` does nothing. Otherwise it deletes all rows with that `C_STRUCTURE_ID` (for 0 or an ID outside the 32-bit range it deletes nothing and only logs a warning) and records one audit group with instance ID 0, empty module key, the given structure ID and description `action`=`uninstallAllForStructure`, `loggedInUserKey`; the audit group is recorded even when no rows existed.

`isAutosyncEnabled(id)` is true exactly when an `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row with that `ID` has `C_ENABLED` true (read through a cached set of enabled IDs). Null gives false without other work; an unknown ID gives false; when the set cannot be loaded it logs a warning and returns false.

`setAutosyncEnabled(null, x)` does nothing. Otherwise it throws `StructureSynchronizerException`: `sync instance #<id> not found` when the instance cannot be loaded (no row, or its parameters cannot be restored); `synchronizer module <moduleKey> is not enabled` when no module with its key is registered; `synchronizer <sync> is not currently available` when `isAvailable()` is false; `synchronizer <sync> does not support autosync` when `isAutosyncSupported()` is false. These checks apply to disabling too, so an instance whose module is missing cannot be disabled; nothing is changed when it throws.

A successful `setAutosyncEnabled(id, enabled)` writes `C_ENABLED`=enabled, so `isAutosyncEnabled(id)` returns enabled at once. When enabling, an 'autosync enabled' marker is handed to the sync-events-manager (on Data Center it records the structure's latest history version, so the instance reacts only to changes from then on). Calling it with the current value is not an error and repeats the write, the marker and the audit record.

After `setAutosyncEnabled` the module records an audit group for the instance with description keys `action`=`setAutosyncEnabled`, `enabled` (the boolean), `loggedInUserKey`, `parameters` (the instance's restored parameter object, an empty map when null).

The module can disable all synchronizers of one structure (used when a structure is archived): it calls `setAutosyncEnabled(id, false)` for every instance in `getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure(structureId)`; an instance that fails (for example its module is missing or does not support autosync) is logged and skipped, the rest are still disabled.

`resync(id, andEnable, processId)` throws `StructureSynchronizerException`: `instanceId == null` for a null ID; for 0 `invalid sync instance id 0`; `sync instance #<id> not found` when no row exists; the restore error when the parameters cannot be restored; `synchronizer <sync or null> is not available` when the module is not registered or `isAvailable()` is false; `... does not support autosync` when andEnable is true and the synchronizer does not support it; `user [userKey=<key>] could not be found, cannot resync instance #<id>` when Jira's user manager has no user with the owner key. Nothing is queued or changed when it throws.

A successful `resync` does not run the synchronizer in the calling thread: it queues a resync request (on Data Center an `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_EVENT` row of type 127) carrying the instance ID, structure ID, module key, owner key, stored parameter text and process ID, and returns. Without andEnable it changes nothing else and records no audit group.

`resync(id, true, p)` also sets `C_ENABLED` true at once (so `isAutosyncEnabled` is immediately true) after queuing the request, without recording an 'autosync enabled' marker, and records an audit group for the instance with description `action`=`enableAfterResync`, `loggedInUserKey`, `parameters`.
Several resync requests for the same installed instance queued before the next sync job pass are merged: only the last one runs. One-time requests (`resyncOnce`) are never merged; each one runs.

`resyncOnce(sync, params, structureId, user, processId)` throws `StructureSynchronizerException` `invalid structure ID <id>` for a null or non-positive structure ID, `null user` for a null user, `synchronizer <sync> is not currently available` when unavailable, `... is not registered` when its module key is not registered, and the store errors when parameters cannot be stored. A null synchronizer throws `NullPointerException` (as the original does).

A successful `resyncOnce` queues a one-time resync run as the given user with instance ID 0; it creates no `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row and records no audit group at request time. During the run the `SyncInstance` given to the synchronizer has ID 0, and Jira and structure changes it makes are not attributed to any synchronizer instance.

`updateSynchronizer(id, params, user)` throws `StructureSynchronizerException`: `instanceId == null` for null; the not-found / invalid-ID / restore errors as `resync` does; `sync instance #<id> must be disabled to edit` when the instance's autosync is enabled; `cannot update sync instance #<id>: <moduleKey> is not available` when no module with its key is registered (the synchronizer's `isAvailable()` is not checked); store errors from `storeParameters`.

`updateSynchronizer` stores the new owner key when user is non-null and the newly stored parameter text when params is non-null; a value that is blank after storing leaves that column unchanged. With both null nothing is written. It returns a new instance read back from the row, whose `getParameters()` is the synchronizer's `restoreParameters` of the stored text (a fresh object, not the one passed in).

Every successful `updateSynchronizer`, even with both arguments null, records an audit group for the returned instance with description keys in order `action`=`edit`, `changedOwner` (user non-null), `changedParameters` (params non-null), `ownerKey` (the owner key after the update), `loggedInUserKey`, `parameters` (the restored parameters).

For Jira's user anonymisation the module lists one entity per instance whose `C_OWNER` is the user's key, with description i18n key `s.anonymize.sync-instance.description` (argument: the instance ID), link `secure/StructureSync.jspa?id=<structure ID>` and link text key `s.anonymize.sync-instance.link`.

Transferring ownership from one user to another processes each instance owned by the first user: it disables autosync, sets the owner to the second user, and enables autosync again if it was enabled before (audit groups for each step). Any `StructureSynchronizerException` (for example a synchronizer that does not support autosync or whose module is missing, since disabling is attempted for every instance) adds the error message of i18n key `s.anonymize.sync-instance.failed` (argument: the instance ID) to the returned result and leaves that instance's owner unchanged (as the original does); the other instances are still processed.

After the plugin stops, the methods throw `StructureStoppedException`, except calls given a null ID (`getInstalledSynchronizer`, `getInstalledSynchronizersForStructure`, `uninstallSynchronizer`, `uninstallSynchronizersForStructure`, `isAutosyncEnabled`, `setAutosyncEnabled`) which return their null result first, and the argument checks that `installSynchronizer`, `installSynchronizerOffline` and `resyncOnce` make before touching storage.

The first method call that reaches storage before the plugin start has run performs the start itself (once; concurrent callers wait up to 180 seconds for it). Starting schedules the sync job (first pass immediately, then every `structure.sync.autosync.interval` ms, default 2000; a value of 0 or less schedules no job, so nothing ever runs automatically) and, on Data Center, tries to become the single node that runs synchronizers.

At start the module subscribes to Jira issue changes and structure changes only when the dark feature `structure.feature.synchronizers.enabled` is on or at least one `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_INSTANCE` row exists; this is decided once, so a synchronizer installed later in the same plugin lifetime gets no change events until restart (as the original does). Each Jira change is recorded with the current time and the ID of the instance whose run is making it (none outside a run); each structure history entry is recorded as a structure event.

On stop the module unsubscribes from issue and structure changes, cancels the sync job, waits up to `structure.sync.stopSynchronizationJobTimeout` ms (default 10000) for a running pass to finish (logging a warning on timeout) and on Data Center releases the synchronizer-node role.

A sync job pass does nothing when another pass is still running, when Active Objects is locked (for example during restore), when a full Jira reindex makes index use impossible, or on Data Center when this node is not the synchronizer node.

Each pass runs incremental sync for the instances with `C_ENABLED` true whose module is registered, `isAvailable()` and `isAutosyncSupported()`; instances whose module is missing or unavailable are skipped (logged) and picked up again in a later pass once the module is back. Without the system setting `structure.sync.order` the order is that of the enabled IDs, ascending.

When `structure.sync.order` is set, enabled instances run in that order: a comma-separated list of instance IDs, short names `links`, `agile`, `subtasks`, `filter`, `rollup` (the five built-in synchronizer module keys) or complete module keys (containing `:`); the value `true` means `links,agile,subtasks,filter,rollup`. Instances matching an earlier element run first; unmatched ones run last; the sort is stable. Unknown elements are logged and ignored.

In a pass, an enabled instance with a pending resync request runs that resync instead of its incremental sync. After all enabled instances, the remaining instance resync requests (for disabled instances) and then the one-time requests run, in request order.

Every run (incremental or resync) executes as the owner: the module looks the owner key up with Jira's user manager and runs with that user as the current Structure user; when the user is not found the run is skipped with a warning (no audit group, the process status is not changed). The forest given to the synchronizer is the structure's skeleton forest secured for the owner; when the structure is missing or not accessible to the owner the run is skipped with a warning.

While a synchronizer runs, `SyncLogger.get()` on that thread returns a logger for the run (cleared afterwards) and the thread name has the run's log prefix appended (restored afterwards). Jira changes the run makes are attributed to the instance (positive IDs only), and structure history entries it writes carry the instance ID as `C_SYNCHRONIZER`.

When a resync request carries a process ID, the background process is set to `ProcessStatus.RUNNING` when the synchronizer starts and to `ProcessStatus.FINISHED` when it ends, also when it fails. When the run is skipped before starting (module unavailable, owner missing, structure inaccessible, parameters not restorable) the status is not changed.

A queued resync looks the synchronizer module up by key when it runs and restores the parameters captured at request time; when the module is not registered or not available, or the parameters cannot be restored, the run is skipped with a warning. It calls the synchronizer's `resync(instance, forestSource)`.

When the synchronizer throws, the error is logged and, only if `SyncAuditLog.isActionGroupRecorded(null)` is true, a failure group is recorded for the instance with the description from `SyncAuditLogHelper.createAuditLogEntryDescription` plus `SyncAuditLogHelper.getFailureDescription` (sync data only for incremental runs). For a `StructureException` that `SyncLogger.warnStructureException` explains, the description has that text as `reason` and no `exception`; otherwise the exception is included. A failure never stops the pass: the next instance still runs.

An incremental run calls the synchronizer's `sync(instance, data, forestSource)` with the Jira change events and the structure change events (only those for the instance's structure) that arrived since its previous run, excluding events caused by this same instance. When there are no such events the synchronizer is not called.

Events are passed on at once by default. With `structure.sync.mindelay` (ms, default 0) positive, a run is postponed while the newest pending event is younger than that delay, unless the oldest pending event is at least `structure.sync.maxdelay` ms old (default 15000; 0 or less disables this override); postponed events are kept for the next pass.

Instead of an incremental run the module runs a full resync of the instance in the same pass when more than `structure.sync.autosync.maxJiraChanges` (default 10000) Jira events are pending for it, or when the structure events exceed both `structure.sync.autosync.maxStructureChangesFixed` (default 10000) and `structure.sync.autosync.maxStructureChangesCoeff` (default 2) times the current forest size.

Cycle guard: when an instance has run incrementally `structure.sync.guard.maxAutosyncsWithoutUserChanges` times in a row (default 10) only because of changes made by another synchronizer instance, with no change by a user in between, and its previous runs did make changes, the run is skipped and the pair is reported as a cycle. Unless `structure.sync.guard.stop.disable` is set, both instances get autosync disabled at the end of the pass. `structure.sync.guard.disable` turns the guard off.

When outgoing mail is configured, a detected cycle sends mail template `sync-cycle` to the active owners of both instances (at most once per `structure.sync.guard.email.admin.interval` ns per instance, default one day; off with `structure.sync.guard.email.owner.disable`) and to Jira's active system administrators after `structure.sync.guard.email.admin.cycles` cycles (default 1) and the same interval (off with `structure.sync.guard.email.admin.disable`). The mail says whether the instances were stopped and gives the limit; no mail is sent when either synchronizer module is unavailable.

When an enabled instance first starts in the sync job and its synchronizer is one of the plugin's own that can verify instances, the configuration is verified as the owner; verification errors send mail template `sync-error` to the owner when active (none to an inactive owner). When verification itself throws, the instance is uninstalled.

None of the `StructureSyncManager` methods checks the caller's permissions on the structure or Synchronization app permission; the only user checks are that an owner exists (install offline, resync, at run time).
`recordActions(instance, description, actions)` records the group with `instance.getId()`, `instance.getSynchronizerModuleKey()` and `instance.getStructureId()`, exactly as the explicit-ID form.

`recordActions` does not write to the database: it timestamps the group with the current time and queues it; a null actions list becomes empty. The queue is written by a background job every `structure.sync.audit.pendingRecordsWriteInterval` ms (default 30000), so `getActions` sees a group only after the next write.

With `structure.sync.audit.pendingRecordsWriteInterval` set to 0, `recordActions` ignores every group (logged at info) and no write job is started. A negative value queues groups but never writes them.
When more than 1,000,000 groups are pending, `recordActions` first drops the oldest pending groups down to 1,000,000 (logging an error with the number dropped), then queues the new one.

A write pass does nothing while Active Objects is locked (pending groups stay queued). It drops groups with no actions unless the dark feature `structure.sync.audit.writingEmptyGroups` is on at write time.

Each written group becomes one `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_AUDIT_RECORD` header row (`C_GROUP_ID` 0, `C_SYNC_INSTANCE`, `C_SYNC_MODULE_KEY` with empty stored as null, `C_STRUCTURE_ID`, `C_TIMESTAMP`, `C_DATA` the description's JSON text or null) followed by one row per non-null action, in order, with the same `C_SYNC_INSTANCE` and `C_TIMESTAMP`, `C_GROUP_ID` the header's `ID`, `C_DATA` the action's JSON text, and no module key or structure ID.
`isActionGroupRecorded` reads the dark feature `structure.sync.audit.writingEmptyGroups` on each call: true for a non-empty list, otherwise (null or empty) the feature's value.

`getActions(instanceId, structureId, from, to)` reads `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_AUDIT_RECORD` rows filtered by `C_SYNC_INSTANCE`=instanceId only when it is positive, `C_STRUCTURE_ID`=structureId only when positive, `C_TIMESTAMP` >= from only when from > `Long.MIN_VALUE`, and `C_TIMESTAMP` <= to only when to < `Long.MAX_VALUE`; and returns the groups sorted by timestamp, newest first (groups with equal timestamps keep their read order).

Each returned group has the header row's instance ID, module key (empty string when the column is null), structure ID, timestamp and description (null when `C_DATA` is null or not valid JSON), and as actions the read rows whose `C_GROUP_ID` is that header's `ID`, in read order; an action row with null or unparsable `C_DATA` is left out. Action rows whose header is not among the read rows are not returned.

Because action rows have no `C_STRUCTURE_ID`, `getActions` with a positive structure ID returns the matching groups with empty action lists (as the original does); filtering by instance ID keeps the actions.

`getActions` reads at most `structure.sync.audit.queryLimit` rows (default 10000), headers and actions counted together, with no ORDER BY, so the rows kept are the first ones the database returns, not necessarily the newest; a group may come back with only part of its actions.

The module's purge (used by maintenance task `removeOldSyncAuditLogRecords`) deletes every `AO_8BAD1B_SYNC_AUDIT_RECORD` row with `C_TIMESTAMP` strictly less than the given epoch milliseconds, header and action rows alike, and logs the count.

Every `loadAttributeValues` variant returns at once without calling the receiver at all (no values, no `receiveMeta`, no `receiveInaccessibleRows`) when the forest spec / `ItemForest` / `Forest`, the row list or the attribute collection is null. No exception is thrown.

With strict false, a forest spec whose last transformation uses the module `com.almworks.jira.structure:filter-item` is loaded as the spec without that last transformation; then, if the resulting spec has no transformations at all, its unsecured form is used. A spec with other transformations is kept as it is (secured or not). With strict true the given spec is used unchanged. The same adjustment applies to `getAttributeValues(ForestSpec, boolean, ...)` and `getConsistentAttributeValues`.

Unless security is overridden (`StructureAuth.isSecurityOverridden()`), requested rows that the current `StructureAuth` user may not see are excluded before loading and reported once through `receiveInaccessibleRows` with the set of those rows, before any values; the receiver gets no values for them (a delivered column returns null for those rows). A row counts as not visible when its item is hidden from the user by Jira permissions, when its item is not an issue and resolves to nothing (deleted item), or when the row id does not exist. `receiveInaccessibleRows` is not called when every requested row is visible.
When security is overridden for the calling thread, no row is filtered: values are delivered for every requested row that exists in the forest and `receiveInaccessibleRows` is never called.

When the forest spec actually loaded is unsecured (after the non-strict adjustment), rows that a sub-structure inserter produced from a structure the current user cannot VIEW (per `StructureManager` permission of that structure) are treated as inaccessible too, as are rows derived from such rows; with a secured spec this extra check is not done (the secured forest already excludes them). The `ItemForest` and `Forest` variants never do this extra check.

An attribute that cannot be loaded (no loader provider accepts its spec, or building its loader fails) does not abort the call: the receiver gets, for that attribute, a value column in which every row has an up-to-date `AttributeValue.error()` value, followed by `valuesReady` for it; the other attributes load normally. The failure may also appear once in `ValuesMeta.getLoadingErrors()` (one entry per failing attribute, without row or item).

`receiveMeta` is called exactly once, after all values, at the end of a loading that ran to completion. When the receiver's `isCancelled()` returns true the loading stops silently: no exception, and `receiveMeta` is not called.

If the forest of the spec cannot be obtained (the forest service throws `StructureException`, e.g. the structure does not exist or is not accessible), the call does not throw: attributes that depend only on the item are still delivered for the requested rows, forest-dependent attributes get no values, and `receiveMeta` is still called.

When loading has to be restarted because of concurrent cache changes, it is retried; after the configured number of restarts (dark feature `structure.attribute.cleanup.maxLoadingRestartAttempts`, default 10) the call throws `StructureRuntimeException` wrapping the last restart cause. Applies to every loading method, including `getConsistentAttributeValues` and `hasUpdate`.

`loadAttributeValues(Forest, ...)` with a null forest returns without callbacks; `getAttributeValues(Forest, ...)` returns `RowValues.EMPTY` when the forest, rows or attributes are null. For a non-null forest the items of its rows are resolved through the row manager without an item access check at lookup time; visibility of the requested rows is still filtered for the current user (see hidden rows).

For the `ItemForest` and `Forest` variants, forest-dependent values (aggregates, propagations and similar) are computed from the given forest on every call and not reused by a later call, so a second call with a modified forest gives values that reflect the modification; item-only values may come from the shared per-item cache. Rows of the given forest that are temporary (negative or transient ids) are accepted.

The `getAttributeValues` variants never return outdated values: the returned `RowValues` holds, for each requested attribute and requested row, the up-to-date `LoadedValue` (so `isOutdated()` is false), and only requested rows are present. Rows reported inaccessible, and rows not in the forest, have no value (lookup returns null). For an unloadable attribute every requested row maps to an error value, inaccessible rows included.

`getAttributeValues(ForestSpec, boolean, rows, attributes, metaConsumer)` passes the loading's `ValuesMeta` to the consumer once, on the calling thread, before returning; a null consumer is allowed and the meta is then dropped. The consumer is not called when any argument except the consumer is null (`RowValues.EMPTY` is returned).

`getConsistentAttributeValues` obtains the latest forest of the (adjusted) spec from the forest service and calls the rows function with an `ItemForest` for it whose items are looked up without access checks; a null function means all rows of that forest. The rows returned by the function are used as given (they are not filtered to the forest or to visible rows) and are the result's rows; the result's forest is that latest forest. The function may be called again on each retry.

`getConsistentAttributeValues` accepts a loading when, after it, the forest source still reports the same latest forest version and the item-data version is unchanged since the loading; when either changed, it reloads, and it also accepts a reload whose values for every cacheable requested attribute and row equal those of the previous loading. The result carries the forest version and items version reported by the accepted loading's `ValuesMeta`.

When `getConsistentAttributeValues` gives up after the configured number of attempts (dark feature `structure.attribute.maxConsistentLoadAttempts`, read once at construction, default 5), the `StructureException` it throws has error `CONSISTENT_OPERATION_FAILED`. When the forest cannot be obtained (a `StructureException` from the forest service) it returns `ConsistentRowValues.EMPTY` instead of throwing; a cancelled loading also gives `ConsistentRowValues.EMPTY`.

The `ItemValues` returned by `getItemValues` answers `getLoadedValue(item, attribute)` with null for an item that was not in the input collection (or a null item); for an input item it returns what loading gave for that item's row, which is null when the current user may not see the item.

`isItemAttribute` returns true only when the attribute's loader keeps its values in the per-item cache, i.e. the value depends only on the item and the user context; it returns false for null, for an attribute no provider can load (no exception escapes), and for forest-dependent attributes such as aggregates over sub-rows. It loads nothing and calls no receiver.

Both `getAttributeValuesWithUpdateChecker` variants return `RowValues.EMPTY` values and a checker that always answers false when the forest (or spec), the rows or the attributes are null. Otherwise the values are those `getAttributeValues` would return (up to date only), and the checker, given a row list, answers `hasUpdate` for those rows, the same attributes and the meta of this loading (with the spec for the `ForestSpec` variant; with no spec, i.e. item-level checks only, for the `ItemForest` variant).

`hasUpdate` returns false when rows or attributes are null. Otherwise it returns true if the value caches were reset since the loading (cache sequence not comparable, e.g. after the plugin's caches were cleared), if any requested value for the rows' items (or, with a spec, the rows' forest values) is no longer cached, is outdated or was recalculated after the loading, or if the spec's forest cannot be obtained; when the check is cancelled or cannot run it also answers true. It returns false when every relevant cached value is unchanged. With a null spec, forest-dependent attributes are checked only through the item-level values they depend on.

Loading runs for the current `StructureAuth` user: the same request made by two users can give different values and different inaccessible rows; values are cached per user where they depend on the user, and the plugin's per-user cache clear for a user forces that user's values to be recomputed.

`createSubscription` returns a new `AttributeSubscription` whose `getSubscriptionId()` is the next number of a node-local counter starting at 1 when the plugin's component is created (1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps for successful calls), owned by the current `StructureAuth` user (null when anonymous). The new subscription has no attributes and no rows. Calls are serialized, so concurrent callers get distinct ids.

If the subscription cannot be put into the in-memory store, `createSubscription` throws `StructureRuntimeException` (message 'subscription system could not create a subscription'); the id it would have used is not reused.

`getSubscription(id)` for a live subscription of the current user returns the same object that `createSubscription` returned (identity), on every call; ids are never created on lookup, so asking for an id that was not created yet (e.g. the next one) fails and does not reserve it.

`getSubscription` throws `StructureException` with error `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` (message 'subscription <id> does not exist') when the id is null, unknown, dropped, expired or evicted, and also when the subscription's owner differs from the current user (the comparison is of the Jira user objects, so an anonymous caller cannot get a logged-in user's subscription and a logged-in user cannot get one created anonymously). The error is the same in all cases, so another user's subscription looks like a missing one.

Subscriptions are kept in a node-local in-memory cache that expires an entry one hour after its last access (dark feature `attribute.subscriptions`, in seconds, default 3600; a JVM system property `structure.cache.expiration-override` replaces it) and holds at most `structure.attribute.maxSubscriptionCount` entries (dark feature read once at start, default 10000), evicting older ones beyond that. `getSubscription` and `dropSubscription` count as access. An expired or evicted subscription is deactivated and its id then fails as unknown. Subscriptions are lost on restart and are not visible from other cluster nodes.

`dropSubscription(id)` throws the same `SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` error as `getSubscription` (null, unknown, or another user's subscription, which is then left untouched); otherwise it removes the subscription so that later `getSubscription`/`dropSubscription` with that id throw that error, and deactivates it.

A deactivated subscription (dropped, expired or evicted) cancels its running loads and forgets its window and values: `getAttributes()` and `getRows()` become empty, `getUpdate(any version)` returns an update with version `DataVersion.ZERO`, not full, whose values are `RowValues.EMPTY` (so `isEmpty()` is true), `loadValues()` returns an already completed future with `DataVersion.ZERO`, `isLoadingValues()` is false, and `changeSubscription` is ignored (logged as a warning, nothing changes). Deactivating twice has no further effect.

A subscription loads its values in a background job (job pool 'attribute') that runs as the subscription's owner, by calling the attribute service's `loadAttributeValues(forestSpec, rows, attributes, receiver)` (non-strict) with the subscription's window, so values and inaccessible rows are those of the owner.

`recordBatch` stores the batch and returns an id whose high 32 bits are a signature chosen at random when the component is created (a value from 0 to 65535, fixed for the life of that runtime instance) and whose low 32 bits are a counter that starts at 1 and grows by one per call, so two consecutive calls on the same instance return ids that differ by 1. It neither copies nor checks the batch (the batch's own `userKey`, set when the `EffectBatch` was constructed, decides who may load it).

`loadBatch(id)` returns the very object passed to `recordBatch` (identity) when the id's high 32 bits equal this instance's signature, the batch is still stored and either the current `StructureAuth` user key equals the batch's `userKey` (anonymous: both null) or security is overridden. It returns null for an id from another runtime signature (for example from before a restart), for an unknown or removed id, and for a batch of another user. It never throws.

Batches are removed only by a periodic job scheduled at plugin start with initial delay and period from dark feature `structure.effect.lifetime.checkInterval` (milliseconds, default 35000). Each run removes the batches whose `timestamp` (the `EffectBatch` field, `System.nanoTime()` at construction unless the caller changed it) is more than dark feature `structure.effect.lifetime` milliseconds old (default 71000). `loadBatch` does not refresh the timestamp and does not check age itself, so a batch stays loadable until the next cleanup run after its lifetime has passed (up to about 106 s by default).

Batches live only in this node's memory and are never persisted; `recordBatch` and `loadBatch` work even before the component is started or after it is stopped (there is no lifecycle check), but nothing expires before start, and stopping cancels the cleanup job. If scheduling the cleanup job fails, the failure is logged and batches never expire.

`startProcess(instances, structureId, requiresConfirmation)` and `validateStartProcess(instances, structureId)` check in this order and throw at the first failure: (1) unless security is overridden, the current user must hold the app permission `executeEffectors` (`CoreAppPermissions.EXECUTE_EFFECTORS` via `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed`), else `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED`; (2) the list must not be empty, else `INVALID_PARAMETER`; then for each instance in list order: (3) an effector with its module key must be installed, else `INVALID_PARAMETER`; (4) its owning structure must not be null, else `INVALID_PARAMETER`; (5) `StructureManager.isAccessible(owningStructure, VIEW)` must be true, else `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for that structure; (6) if the owning structure differs from the given structure id, unless security is overridden the user must hold `executeEffectorsOnQueries`, else `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED`. `validateStartProcess` creates nothing.

`startProcess(moduleKey, parameters, forestSpec, requiresConfirmation)` and its `validateStartProcess` check in order: (1) `executeEffectors` permission, else `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED`; (2) `executeEffectorsOnQueries` permission, else `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` (both skipped when security is overridden); (3) an effector with that complete module key is installed, else `INVALID_PARAMETER`; (4) if the forest spec names a structure, `StructureManager.isAccessible(structureId, VIEW)` must be true, else `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. The effector parameters are not validated at this point.

A successful `startProcess` creates a process handle (an `AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE` row managed by the current user, progress 0) and an `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS` row with `C_STATUS` `PENDING`, `C_USER_KEY` the current user's key, `C_PROCESS_HANDLE_ID` the handle id, `C_CREATED` now, `C_NODE_ID` this node's cluster id (null when not clustered), `C_ACKNOWLEDGED` false and `C_PARAMETERS` holding `structureId` and `effectorInstances` (snapshots of the given instances) for an instance run, or `oneOffEffectorModuleKey`, `oneOffParams` and `oneOffForestSpec` for a one-off run; it returns the new row's ID and schedules the calculation in the background (job pool 'effector'). If the calculation job cannot be scheduled it throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR`, leaving the `PENDING` row in place.

The calculation job runs as the process owner. It first moves the process from `PENDING` to `CALCULATING` (setting `C_START_TIME`; if the row is no longer `PENDING` it does nothing). Then: if the effector produced errors, or an exception was thrown, the status becomes `CALCULATION_FAILED` with the errors stored in the preview's `errors`; if cancellation was requested, `CALCULATION_STOPPED` (preview cleared); if the optimised preview has no effects, `COMPLETED`; if confirmation is required, `CALCULATED` with the preview and `C_FINISH_TIME`; otherwise, if every effect is only a warning, `COMPLETED`; else `QUEUED` with the preview, and `C_QUEUED` and `C_FINISH_TIME` set to the same current time.

When an effector rejects its parameters (its function answers with errors instead of a valid function), the calculation does not fail: each error becomes a warning effect in the preview. A preview made only of such warnings then completes the process (`COMPLETED`) without applying anything, unless confirmation is required, in which case it is stored as `CALCULATED`.

In an instance run the forest is the structure given at start (`ForestSpec.structure(structureId)`), loaded consistently with the attributes the effectors need. Each instance's row is found as the row(s) of item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`/<instance id> in that forest: no such row fails the calculation (`CALCULATION_FAILED`), and more than one row fails it as well. An effector whose module is no longer installed at calculation time also fails it.

Instances of one run are evaluated in order of their row's depth in the forest (shallower first), and for equal depth in forest order; each instance's effects are computed over the sub-forest made of its row's parent and everything under that parent (the whole forest when the instance row is at the top level). Effects of all instances are appended to one preview in that order.

A one-off run evaluates the effector once over the whole latest forest of the given forest spec, with the given parameters (an absent parameter map counts as empty). If the effector's module is not installed when the calculation runs, the process becomes `CALCULATION_FAILED`.

`getProcess(id)` returns the stored snapshot when the process exists and either security is overridden, the current user is a Jira administrator (`StructurePluginHelper.isAdmin`), or the process's user key equals the current user's key. Otherwise, including for an unknown id, it throws `StructureException` with error code 6017 (category `NOT_FOUND`). Every other id-taking method (`getEffectRecords`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `acknowledgeFinished`, `deleteCalculated`, `resumeInterrupted`, `startUndoProcess`) performs this check first and throws the same error.

`getEffectRecords(id)` returns all `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_RECORD` rows of the process as `EffectRecord`s (error and success records alike), an empty list when none were written; an undo effect stored as empty or null reads as null, and affected items read as an empty list when none are stored. Results are cached and refreshed when a record is added.

`confirm(id)` throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_PARAMETER` when the status is not `CALCULATED`, when the process has no preview, or when the preview has no effects. If every preview effect is a warning, it sets the process to `COMPLETED` (preview cleared, finish time set) and returns normally without queuing.
