Otherwise it resets the process handle to pending with 0% progress and moves the process from `CALCULATED` to `QUEUED` (setting `C_QUEUED`); if that conditional update finds the process no longer `CALCULATED`, it throws `GENERIC_ERROR`.

Deprecated `confirm(id, indexes)`: first makes the same checks as `confirm(id)` on the full preview (including completing a warnings-only preview). With non-null indexes it keeps the preview effects at those indexes in the order the collection yields them (duplicate indexes keep duplicate effects, as the original does; indexes below 0 or at or beyond the preview size are dropped); if none remain it throws `INVALID_PARAMETER`; otherwise it replaces the stored preview with that subset (its error list dropped), and if the subset consists only of warnings it completes the process instead of queuing. With null indexes it behaves exactly like `confirm(id)`.

`cancel(id)` looks up the process handle; if it no longer exists it throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR`. Otherwise it marks the handle cancelled (`C_CANCELLED` of the `AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE` row) and returns at once, for a process in any status (no status check). A running calculation then ends `CALCULATION_STOPPED`, a running application `APPLY_STOPPED` after the effect in progress (applied effects are kept), and a queued process whose handle is cancelled stops as `APPLY_STOPPED` as soon as applying begins, before any effect.

`acknowledgeFinished(id)` sets `C_ACKNOWLEDGED` true when the status is `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED` (acknowledging an already acknowledged finished process succeeds again) and the process then no longer appears in `getRunningProcessesForUser`; in any other status it throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` and changes nothing.

`deleteCalculated(id)` deletes the process row and its process handle row when the status is `CALCULATED`, `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `CALCULATION_FAILED`; afterwards `getProcess(id)` throws the not-found error. In any other status (or if the row changed status concurrently) it throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR`.

`resumeInterrupted(id)` moves an `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` process to `QUEUED`, sets `C_QUEUED` to now and `C_ACKNOWLEDGED` to false; when it is applied again, preview effects whose preview index already has a record (success or error) are skipped, and an error record from before the resume still makes the final status `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`. In any other status it throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR`.

`startUndoProcess(id, indexes)` checks in order: the `executeEffectors` permission (unless security is overridden; else `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED`), access to the process (error 6017), status in `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED` (else `INVALID_PARAMETER`), and at least one selected record (else `INVALID_PARAMETER`). Selected records are the non-error records of the process, restricted, when indexes is not null, to those whose preview index is in the collection.

The undo process is a new `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_PROCESS` row owned by the current user whose `C_PARAMETERS` hold `revertedProcessId` and, when the reverted process had them, `structureId` and `oneOffForestSpec`; its preview is the undo effects of the selected records in record order, records without an undo effect being skipped, and it goes from `PENDING` straight to `QUEUED` without calculation or confirmation. If all selected records lack an undo effect the empty preview is still queued and the undo process completes without records (as the original does). `getProcess` of it reports `getRevertedProcessId()` equal to the reverted id.

Applying is done by a job scheduled at component start with delay and period from the JVM system property `structure.effector.apply.interval` (milliseconds, default 2000). Each run takes at most one `QUEUED` process, the one with the smallest `C_QUEUED` (rows with null first), sets it `IN_PROGRESS` with `C_START_TIME` now and `C_FINISH_TIME` null, and applies its whole preview before the run ends. In Jira Data Center only the node holding the cluster-wide 'effector' exclusive work flag applies; a run is skipped while Jira's full reindex blocks index use or Active Objects is locked.

While applying, the job runs as the process owner (without security override) and handles preview effects in index order: warning effects are skipped without a record; an effect whose effect provider is not installed gets an error record; an effect the provider resolves to nothing gets no record; an effect that resolves to an error gets an error record with its affected items; otherwise the effect is applied and a success record stores the provider's success message, the returned undo effect and the affected items. Every record carries `C_PROCESS_ID`, `C_PREVIEW_INDEX` and `C_TIMESTAMP` (now). A failure while applying one effect makes an error record and applying continues with the next effect.

At the end of applying, the process becomes `APPLY_STOPPED` if cancellation was noticed (checked before each effect), else `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS` if any record of the process (including ones written before a resume) is an error, else `COMPLETED`; completion clears `C_EFFECTOR_PREVIEW` and sets `C_FINISH_TIME`. If the owner's user key no longer resolves to a Jira user, or applying throws unexpectedly, the process is set to `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`. If the plugin stops during applying, the process stays `IN_PROGRESS` until restart recovery.

On component start, this node's processes in `PENDING` or `CALCULATING` (matched by `C_NODE_ID`, or with null `C_NODE_ID` on a single-node install) become `CALCULATION_STOPPED`. On the first apply run after start (on the applying node), every `IN_PROGRESS` and every `QUEUED` process becomes `APPLY_INTERRUPTED`, so even a process queued just after start but before that run is interrupted (as the original does); on every later run, any process still `IN_PROGRESS` (left by another node) is put back to `QUEUED`.

`findProcesses(user, status, structureId)` performs no permission check and returns, newest first by `C_CREATED`, the processes matching every non-null filter: `C_USER_KEY` equal to the user's key, `C_STATUS` equal to the status name, and a structure id equal to the run's `structureId` parameter or, when absent, the structure of its `oneOffForestSpec` (undo runs carry the copied value). All nulls return all processes; never null.

`getRunningProcessesForUser(user)` performs no permission check and returns the user's processes with `C_ACKNOWLEDGED` false, newest first by `C_CREATED`, in any status; it is cached per user key and refreshed when the user's processes are created, acknowledged, deleted or re-keyed. A null user throws `NullPointerException`.

Stopping the component cancels the apply job, waits up to the JVM system property `structure.effector.stopApplyJobTimeout` milliseconds (default 10000) for a running apply run to finish, cancels every process handle still being tracked and releases the Data Center 'effector' work flag. Progress of running processes is pushed to their process handles about every 3 seconds (system property `structure.effector.update.interval`, default 3000).

`createEffectorInstance(moduleKey, parameters, owningStructure)` inserts an `AO_8BAD1B_EFFECTOR_INSTANCE` row with `C_MODULE_KEY` the given key (not checked against installed effectors), `C_PARAMETERS` the parameters as compact JSON or null when the map is null or empty, and `C_OWNING_STRUCTURE` the given id (null allowed), and returns the row's auto-increment ID. It checks no permission and records a change of item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`/<new id> with the item tracker.

`getEffectorInstance(id)` returns an `EffectorInstance` with that id, the stored module key, owning structure (null if none) and parameters as an unmodifiable map (an empty map when none are stored). For an id with no row (including ids outside the 32-bit range, which are looked up as 0) it returns null instead of throwing. If reading storage fails it throws an unchecked `StructureRuntimeException`, not a `StructureException`. Results are cached (one hour after last access by default, dark feature `structure.effectorInstance.cache.timeout` in seconds) and the cache entry is dropped on every create, update and delete of that id.

`updateEffectorInstance(id, moduleKey, parameters, owningStructure)` throws `StructureException` with `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` (for item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector`/<id>) when no row has that id; otherwise it overwrites all three columns (null or empty parameters store null, null structure detaches), so a following `getEffectorInstance` returns the new values, and records a change of the instance's item with the item tracker.

`deleteEffectorInstance(id)` deletes the row with that id; only when a row was actually deleted does it drop the cache entry and record a change of the instance's item. Deleting a missing id does nothing and does not throw; forest rows that show the instance are not removed, and `getEffectorInstance` of the deleted id returns null.

After the plugin has stopped, `createEffectorInstance`, `getEffectorInstance`, `updateEffectorInstance` and `deleteEffectorInstance` throw the unchecked `StructureStoppedException` without touching storage; before the plugin has started they work normally.

Each getter of `StructureComponents` returns the plugin's exported component of the matching service: getStructureManager the structure-manager component, getForestService forest-service, getAttributeService attribute-service, getAttributeSubscriptionService attribute-subscription-service, getStructureConfiguration structure-configuration (the same object `StructurePluginHelper.getConfiguration()` returns), getSyncManager sync-manager, getBackupManager backup-manager, getJobManager job-manager, getScheduledJobManager scheduled-job-manager, getIssueEventBridge event-bridge, getViewManager view-manager, getFavoriteManager favorite-manager, getStructureQueryParser structure-query-parser, getStructureQueryBuilderFactory structure-query-builder-factory, getProcessHandleManager process-handle-manager, getRowManager structure-row-manager, getSyncAuditLog sync-audit-log, getGeneratorManager generator-manager, getItemResolver item-resolver, getFolderManager folder-manager, getStructurePropertyService structure-property-service, getItemTracker item-tracker, getEffectorInstanceManager effector-instance-manager and getEffectorProcessManager effector-process-manager. An instance obtained by injection from another plugin is identical (==) to the component injected directly.

The `StructureComponents` bundle takes all 24 services once, when it is constructed, and never replaces them: every getter returns the same non-null instance on every call, from any thread, and calling a getter makes no call on any service (no lazy lookup, no permission check, no dependency on the current user).

The `StructureComponents` component is created by the plugin container with constructor injection of all 24 services listed for its getters; it cannot exist (and so cannot be injected into another plugin) before each of those services has been created. It holds no state of its own beyond these references.

`StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed(permission, user)` answers from a per-permission cache keyed by the user's key (anonymous and a user whose key is null share the key ""): the first answer for a (permission, user key) pair is remembered. All remembered answers are dropped when 5 minutes have passed since they were last dropped (checked on the next access), or when the plugin clears its permission caches (on all cluster nodes). The setters of `StructureConfiguration` do not clear this cache, so after a configuration change `isAllowed` and the default methods built on it (`isStructureAvailableToUser`, `isCreateStructureAllowed`, ...) may return the old answer for up to 5 minutes.

For `CoreAppPermissions.USE`, `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed` returns `StructureConfiguration.isStructureAvailable(user)` (not `StructureConfiguration.isAllowed`). So, unlike the configuration's `isAllowed(USE, null)`, `isAllowed(USE, null)` and `isStructureAvailableToUser(null)` can be true for an anonymous user: for example when the use permission is granted to anyone and the anonymous user can browse a project where the plugin is enabled. `isViewCreationAllowed(null)` stays false.

For `CoreAppPermissions.CREATE_STRUCTURE`, `SYNCHRONIZATION` and `AUTOMATION`, `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed(permission, user)` returns `StructureConfiguration.isAllowed` for the same permission and user (so false for null).

In `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed`, `CONFIGURE_GENERATORS` is true only when the configuration allows both `AUTOMATION` and `CONFIGURE_GENERATORS` to the user; `CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS` only when it allows both `AUTOMATION` and `CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS`; `EXECUTE_EFFECTORS` only when the configuration allows `EXECUTE_EFFECTORS` and the user holds Jira's global Bulk Change permission; `EXECUTE_EFFECTORS_ON_QUERIES` only when all of the `CONFIGURE_EFFECTORS` and `EXECUTE_EFFECTORS` conditions hold and the configuration also allows `EXECUTE_EFFECTORS_ON_QUERIES`. Example: with every permission granted to anyone, a user without Bulk Change gets false for both execute permissions.

In `StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed`, `MANAGE_GLOBAL_SAVED_COLUMNS` is true only when the user holds Jira's global 'create shared objects' permission and the configuration allows `MANAGE_GLOBAL_SAVED_COLUMNS` to the user; so `isManageGlobalSavedColumnsAllowed` is false for a user without that Jira permission even if the plugin permission is granted to anyone.

`StructurePluginHelper.isAllowed` with a `StructureAppPermission` whose key is not one of the nine `CoreAppPermissions` keys throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message "Unknown permission: <key>"; permissions are matched by key, not by identity.

`isAdmin(user)` and `isSystemAdmin(user)` ask Jira's `GlobalPermissionManager` for `GlobalPermissionKey.ADMINISTER` and `GlobalPermissionKey.SYSTEM_ADMIN` on every call (no caching); `hasPermission(GlobalPermissionKey, user)` asks it for the given key with the user as given, including null, without a null shortcut.

`hasPermission(ProjectPermissionKey, Issue, user)` and `hasPermission(ProjectPermissionKey, Project, user)` return Jira `PermissionManager.hasPermission` for that permission, object and user (null user passed through), and false without asking Jira when the issue or project is null.

`isIssueEditable(issue, user)` returns Jira `IssueManager.isEditable(issue, user)` (which honours workflow restrictions). When the dark feature `structure.permissions.ignore.workflow` was true at the time the helper was created, it instead returns whether the user holds the Edit Issues project permission on the issue; changing the property later has no effect until the plugin restarts. A null issue gives false in both modes.

`getIssueError(Long, checkEdit, user)` converts only a Jira `DataAccessException` thrown while reading the issue into its returned error (and logs it); any other runtime exception from `IssueManager.getIssueObject` propagates to the caller.

`isProjectStructuredForCurrentUser(project)` takes the user from `StructureAuth.getUser()`. Unless security is overridden in `StructureAuth`, it first asks Jira `PermissionManager.hasPermission(BROWSE_PROJECTS, project, user)` and returns false if denied; it then returns `StructureConfiguration.isProjectEnabled(project)`. With security overridden only the enablement is checked.

`getUser()` returns Jira `JiraAuthenticationContext.getLoggedInUser()` on every call, ignoring any user set through `StructureAuth`; so `getStructureProjectsForCurrentUser()`, `getProjectsForCurrentUser()`, `getAvailableGroupsForCurrentUser()` and `getI18n()` act for the Jira-logged-in user even inside a `StructureAuth` sudo.

`getStructureProjectsForCurrentUser()` returns the projects of `StructureConfiguration.getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()` that `getUser()` may browse (Browse Projects through Jira's `PermissionManager`), in the same order; `getProjectsForCurrentUser()` does the same for all projects from `ProjectManager.getProjectObjects()`. Neither honours a `StructureAuth` security override; both return a new list.

`filterInvisibleProjects` looks each project ID up with Jira `ProjectManager.getProjectObj`; only a Jira `DataAccessException` from the lookup is caught (logged, and the ID counts as invisible). IDs are reported in input order and a duplicated invisible ID is reported once per occurrence.

`searchQuery(String)` and `searchAndSortQuery(String)` return an empty array for null, empty or whitespace-only text without parsing it; otherwise they parse the text with Jira's `JqlQueryParser` (a `JqlParseException` propagates) and continue as the `Query` variant.

`searchQuery(Query)`, `searchAndSortQuery(Query)` and `searchAndSortQuery(Query, limit)` search the Jira index as the user from `StructureAuth.getUser()`, ignoring issue security when `StructureAuth.isSecurityOverridden()` is true; a null query gives an empty array. `searchAndSortQuery(Query)` is `searchAndSortQuery(Query, 0)` (no limit). When Jira reports that the index cannot be used (full reindex running or index inconsistent), they return an empty array without searching and log a warning (rate-limited). A `SearchException` from Jira propagates.

`matchIssues(issues, query, collectMatching, collector)` sorts and de-duplicates an unsorted input (the caller's list is not modified) before matching, then behaves as the six-argument `matchIssuesSorted` with the user and security-override flag from `StructureAuth`; so each ID is reported at most once. Null or empty input reports nothing.

In `matchIssuesSorted` (both forms) and `matchIssues`, when Jira reports that the index cannot be used, no search is run: with collectMatching false every input ID is added to the collector, with collectMatching true nothing is added.

`matchIssuesSorted` given input that is not sorted ascending: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws `AssertionError` before searching; with assertions disabled the result is undefined. Sorted input with duplicates passes the check.

The six-argument `matchIssuesSorted(issues, query, collectMatching, user, overrideSecurity, collector)` searches as the given user (null = anonymous) and honours the given override flag, not `StructureAuth`. With a null query, an input ID matches when the user can see the issue (or it exists, with override); IDs of missing or invisible issues are reported only in non-matching mode.
`validateQuery(user, query)` returns Jira `SearchService.validateQuery(user, query)` unchanged.

`requireResource(key)` calls the platform web-resource manager's requireResource with the key unchanged; `requireResourcesForContext(context)` requires that context; `requireResourceIfPresent(key)` first asks `PluginAccessor.getPluginModule(key)` and requires the resource only when that returns non-null.

`requireQuickEditResources()` requires, each only if present, `com.atlassian.jira.jira-quick-edit-plugin:quick-edit-issue` then `com.atlassian.jira.jira-quick-edit-plugin:quick-create-issue`. `requireIssueShortcuts()` asks Jira's `KeyboardShortcutManager` for the shortcuts of the `issueaction` and then the `issuenavigation` contexts.

`requireIssueDetailsResources()` requires the web-resource context `jira.view.issue`, then the resource `com.almworks.jira.structure:issue-details`, then puts page metadata `viewissue-use-history-api` = `false`.

`requireWidgetResource()` does, in this order: the quick-edit resources (as `requireQuickEditResources`), Jira's field-resource inclusion for the current user (`FieldsResourceIncluder.includeFieldResourcesForCurrentUser`), resources `com.almworks.jira.structure:widget` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:structure-info`, the context `structure.widget`, resources `com.almworks.jira.structure:details-providers` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:planningTaskCreationDialog`, and finally the issue-details resources (as `requireIssueDetailsResources`).

`requireLocalizedResource(key)` requires the key, then takes the locale from Jira's `JiraAuthenticationContext.getLocale()` (not from `StructureAuth`); with a null locale nothing more is done. Otherwise it requires, each only if a module with that key is present: `key-<language>` if the language is non-empty; `key-<country>` if the country is non-empty and not equal (case-sensitively) to the language string; `key-<language>-<country>` if the country is non-empty; `key-<language>-<country>-<variant>` if the variant is non-empty (even with an empty country, giving `key-<language>--<variant>`). Example: locale de_DE requires `key`, then checks `key-de`, `key-DE`, `key-de-DE`.
`getStaticResourcePrefix()` returns the platform web-resource URL provider's static resource prefix for URL mode AUTO, unchanged.

`getI18n(user)` returns Jira's `I18nHelper.BeanFactory.getInstance(user)` (null user passed through). `getCollator(user)` returns a fresh `Collator.getInstance(locale)` for that helper's locale on every call. `getLocale()` returns the locale of the I18n helper for `StructureAuth.getUser()` (so it honours a `StructureAuth` sudo, unlike `getI18n()`).

The service getters of `StructurePluginHelper` (`getAuthenticationContext`, `getIssueManager`, `getPermissionManager`, `getPluginAccessor`, `getEventManager`, `getProjectManager`, `getProjectRoleManager`, `getUserManager`, `getJqlStringSupport`, `getJqlQueryParser`, `getSearchService`, `getJqlOperandResolver`, `getSearchRequestManager`, `getGlobalPermissionManager`, `getTimeTrackingConfiguration`, `getUserPreferencesManager`, `getCustomFieldManager`) return the Jira or platform component injected into the helper at construction, the same instance on every call, with no permission check. `getConfiguration()` returns the structure-configuration component and `getCacheHelper()` the plugin's `StructureCacheHelper`.

`isStructureLocked()` reports, on each call, whether the plugin's database-wide maintenance lock is currently held (it is taken while a backup is being restored and released afterwards); it does not wait for the lock or take it.

`instantiate(clazz)` asks Jira's `ComponentClassManager.newInstanceFromPlugin(clazz, plugin)` with the plugin of key `com.almworks.jira.structure`, returning a new instance each call with its constructor dependencies injected; exceptions from Jira propagate unchanged.

Permission settings are stored in Jira application properties as a pair per permission: `USE` in `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.enabledForAnyone` and `...config.enabledSubjects`; `CREATE_STRUCTURE` in `...config.createForAnyone` and `...config.creatorSubjects`; `SYNCHRONIZATION` in `...config.synchronizationForAnyone` and `...config.synchronizationSubjects`; `AUTOMATION` in `...config.automationForAnyone` and `...config.automationSubjects`; each other `CoreAppPermissions` constant in `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.permission.<key>.anyone` and `...permission.<key>.subjects` (e.g. `...permission.executeEffectors.anyone`). `setAllowedForAnyone` writes `true` or `false`; `setPermissionSubjectsEncoded` writes the given text (null as empty).

`isEnabledForAllProjects()` and `isAllowedForAnyone(permission)` read their property with a default-backed lookup: absent means true; a stored value means true only if it equals `true` ignoring case (`TRUE` is true; `yes`, `1` or empty text are false). `setEnabledForAllProjects` writes `true` or `false` to `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.enabledForAllProjects`.

Settings that can be long (`com.almworks.jira.structure.config.enabledProjects`, every permission `...Subjects`/`.subjects` key, `...config.defaultStructurePP` and `...config.attributeSensitivity`) are written in pieces of at most 250 characters: the first piece under the key itself, then under `<key>.1`, `<key>.2`, ...; any existing higher-numbered pieces left from a longer earlier value are set to null. On read the pieces from `<key>`, `<key>.1`, ... are concatenated until a missing or empty one. A 600-character value is stored as 250 + 250 + 100 characters in `<key>`, `<key>.1`, `<key>.2`.

Settings are cached in memory without expiry after the first read; every setter writes Jira's application properties and then drops its own cached entry, so the next getter call reflects the change. A value changed directly in Jira's application properties (not through this component) is not seen until the plugin's caches are cleared. The setters perform no permission check and publish no events.

If loading a setting fails, the getter logs a warning and returns a fallback instead of throwing: `isEnabledForAllProjects()` false (unlike the absent-value default of true), `isAllowedForAnyone` true, `getPermissionSubjects` empty, `getPickedProjectIds` empty, default structures none (0), UI settings the built-in defaults and attribute sensitivity `ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean.DEFAULT`.

`getPickedProjectIds()` splits the stored `enabledProjects` text on commas, trims entries and skips blank ones. If the first usable entry is numeric, only numeric entries are taken (keys after it are ignored); if it is a key of an existing project (matched ignoring case through `ProjectManager.getProjectObjByKeyIgnoreCase`), only further keys are taken and later numeric entries are looked up as keys. Unknown keys are skipped and do not decide the kind. The result is sorted ascending without duplicates. Examples: `10101, 10000,10101` gives [10000, 10101]; `10000,ABC` gives [10000]; `abc,10000` gives [id of ABC]. Numeric IDs are not checked for existence.

`getPickedProjects()` returns, in the order of Jira `ProjectManager.getProjectObjects()`, those projects whose ID is among `getPickedProjectIds()`; IDs with no project are left out; with no picked IDs Jira's project list is not read and an empty list is returned. `getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()` returns `ProjectManager.getProjectObjects()` when enabled for all projects, otherwise `getPickedProjects()`. `isProjectEnabled(project)` is true for any non-null project when enabled for all projects; otherwise true only when the project's ID is non-null and among the picked IDs.
`setPickedProjectIds(String)` stores the text exactly as given (null as empty), with no validation, trimming or conversion of keys to IDs; it does not change `isEnabledForAllProjects`.

`getPermissionSubjects(permission)` splits the stored text on commas, trims each piece, skips empty pieces and pieces that `PermissionSubject.fromEncodedString` cannot parse, and returns the rest in stored order. Example: `anyone, ,???` read back gives one subject, the `PermissionSubject.Anyone`.

`isAllowedForAnyone`, `getPermissionSubjects`, `setAllowedForAnyone` and `setPermissionSubjectsEncoded` with a `StructureAppPermission` whose key is not one of the nine `CoreAppPermissions` keys throw `IllegalArgumentException` with message "Unknown permission: <key>" and store nothing. `isAllowed(unknownPermission, user)` returns false without error for a null user or a user failing `isStructureAvailable`, and otherwise throws the same exception.

`isStructureAvailable(user)` is false for every user, Jira administrators included, when the plugin is not enabled for all projects and the stored picked-project ID list is empty. A non-empty list of IDs that match no existing project does not trigger this rule (the browse check later fails instead, except for administrators).

In `isStructureAvailable` and `isAllowed`, a user holding Jira's global Administer permission (asked of `GlobalPermissionManager`, never for null) is accepted without subject or project-browse checks, unless the dark feature `structure.permissions.jiraAdminHasAllPermissions` was false when the component was created (default true); then administrators are treated like everyone else.

For a non-administrator, `isStructureAvailable(user)` requires (unless the use permission is granted to anyone) that some stored use subject matches the user; an anonymous user is matched by the `anyone` subject, never by a group subject or by a user subject naming a user. Then, when enabled for all projects, it returns Jira `PermissionManager.hasProjects(BROWSE_PROJECTS, user)`, and false if that call throws; otherwise it is true only if one of `PermissionManager.getProjects(BROWSE_PROJECTS, user)` is enabled (null or empty gives false). The anonymous user can therefore be available.

When not enabled for all projects, the project clause of `addConfigurationScopeClause` / `getConfigurationScopeQuery` lists the IDs of `getCurrentlyEnabledProjects()` in Jira's project order; picked IDs of projects that no longer exist are left out, and if none remain the clause uses the impossible project ID 2147483647.

The global default structure is written to `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.defaultStructure` as a decimal (null as `0`) and read back with an unparsable value as 0. Project defaults are kept in `...config.defaultStructurePP` as comma-separated `<projectId>=<structureId>` pairs: setting one rewrites the whole list, keeping existing pairs in their order and appending a new project at the end; a change of an existing project's value keeps its position. When reading, a project key (case-insensitive) is accepted in place of the ID, pairs whose project is unknown or whose IDs are not positive, or which contain no `=` or start with it, are ignored, and for a repeated project the last pair wins.

`setDefaultStructureId(project, id)` writes nothing when the project already has that same default, or when the ID is null and the project has no own default. Setting a project default to 0 or a negative ID stores the pair, but it is ignored when read back, so afterwards the project falls back to the global default and `isDefaultStructureSetForProject(project)` is false.

`getDefaultStructureId` and `isDefaultStructureSetForProject` for a non-null project whose `getId()` is null look up the global entry: `getDefaultStructureId` returns the global default and `isDefaultStructureSetForProject` returns true even when no default is set at all (as the original does).

`setUISettings(null, project, s)` writes system settings to Jira application properties and `setUISettings(user, project, s)` writes to the user's Jira property set (`UserPropertyManager.getPropertySet(user)`), under the same keys: `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.issuePage.autoSwitch` from `s.getAutoSwitchStrategy(ISSUE_VIEW)`, `...config.projectPage.autoSwitch` from `s.getAutoSwitchStrategy(PROJECT_TAB)` (as the codes `off`, `withIssue`, `default`), `...config.issuePage.autoCollapse` from `getAutoCollapseStructurePanel()` and `...config.issuePage.keepWhileNavigating` from `getKeepStructureWhileNavigating()` (as `true`/`false`). A null value leaves its key unchanged. A `PropertyException` from the user property set is logged and swallowed. The change is visible to the next `getUISettings` call.

`getUISettings(user, project)` resolves each of the four values separately: the user's own stored value if set, else the system value, else the built-in default. A stored strategy code other than `off`, `withIssue` or `default` (case-sensitive) counts as unset for the user and as the built-in default for the system; a stored boolean counts as true only if it equals `true` ignoring case. For a null user only system values apply.

In the `UISettings` returned by `getUISettings`, `getAutoSwitchStrategy` gives the issue-page value for `ISSUE_VIEW`, the project-page value for `PROJECT_TAB`, `VERSION_TAB` and `COMPONENT_TAB`, always `AUTOSWITCH_OFF` for `GREENHOPPER_TAB`, and always `STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE` for every other page (`STRUCTURE_BOARD`, `STRUCTURE_BOARD_WITH_DETAILS`, `ISSUE_NAVIGATOR`, `GADGET`), whatever is stored.

`clearUISettings(user, project)` removes the four UI keys (`...issuePage.autoSwitch`, `...projectPage.autoSwitch`, `...issuePage.autoCollapse`, `...issuePage.keepWhileNavigating`) from the user's Jira property set, logs and swallows a `PropertyException`, and drops the user's cached settings; with a null user it does nothing.

Per-user UI settings are cached per user key and dropped 1 hour after last access (the dark feature `structure.userconfig.cache.timeout`, in seconds, changes this); so a change made to a user's properties outside this component may stay invisible to `getUISettings` until then or until the user's caches are cleared.

`setAttributeSensitivitySettings(s)` stores JSON `{"sensitivityMode":<code>,"nonSensitiveAttributes":[...]}` under `com.almworks.jira.structure.config.attributeSensitivity` (mode code 0 STANDARD, 1 STRICT, 2 PERMISSIVE; each attribute as its REST spec, in no guaranteed order), then asks `StructureCacheHelper.clearAllStructureCachesOnAllNodes()`. `getAttributeSensitivitySettings()` returns `ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean.DEFAULT` for absent, empty or unparsable JSON; JSON without a mode gives `STANDARD`; an unknown code such as 7 gives `STANDARD` with the stored attributes kept; a missing attribute list gives none.

As a `CachingComponent`, `clearCaches()` drops every cached global and per-user setting so the next getter reloads from Jira properties; `clearUserCaches(user)` and `clearUserCaches(userKey)` drop only that user's cached UI settings.

`getHistoryEntries(structureId, from, to)` (all three forms: streaming, list, and `getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges`) returns the structure's AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY rows whose version is strictly greater than `from` and at most `to`, in ascending version order. With entries at versions 1..5, `(s, 2, 4)` gives versions 3 and 4; `(s, 0, 5)` gives 1..5. Entries of other structures are never included.
In `getHistoryEntries`/`getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges`, a negative `from` means from the very first entry: the range then also includes an entry stored with version 0, which `from` = 0 excludes.

`getHistoryEntries`/`getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges` throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `to` < `from` or `to` < 0 (e.g. `(s, 5, 3)` or `(s, -1, -1)`), before touching the database. When `from` == `to` (and `to` >= 0) nothing is read: the list forms return an empty list and the streaming form never calls the consumer.

`getHistoryEntries`, `getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges`, `getLatestHistoryEntryVersion`, `getEarliestHistoryEntryVersionGtEqDate`, `getEntryCount` and `getEntryCountGtEqDate` do not consult the current user's permissions or `StructureAuth`: an anonymous caller gets the same results as an administrator, and a structure ID with no history (or that does not exist) simply yields no entries / 0.

The streaming `getHistoryEntries(s, from, to, consumer)` passes each entry to `HistoryConsumer.consume` in ascending version order and stops reading as soon as the consumer returns false (no further entries are delivered and no exception is thrown).

Each returned `HistoryEntry` carries the structure ID and version unpacked from AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY.C_ID, `getPrevVersion` = C_PREV_VERSION, `getTimestamp` = C_TIMESTAMP, `getUserKey` = C_USER_KEY (null stays null) and `getSynchronizer` = C_SYNCHRONIZER (null for manual changes). Its change list is unmodifiable and holds one `HistoryEntry.Change` per AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE row with C_HID = that C_ID, in ascending C_ID order.

Each `HistoryEntry.Change` is decoded from its AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE row: C_OPERATION 1/2/3/4 gives ADD/COPY/MOVE/REMOVE, C_FOREST gives the forest, C_PATH_FROM/C_AFTER_FROM/C_PATH_TO/C_AFTER_TO/C_ORIGINAL_ROWS give the row ID lists (a null column gives a null list, e.g. `getPathFrom()` is null for an ADD), and `getDirection()` is C_DIRECTION, or 0 when the column is null.

`getHistoryEntriesWithoutChanges` returns the same entries (same range, order and header fields) as `getHistoryEntries` but every entry's `getChanges()` is an empty list, even when AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE rows exist for it.

When a stored change cannot be decoded (an unknown C_OPERATION code or malformed JSON in a forest or row-list column), a warning is logged and reading stops silently: the entry holding that change and all later entries of the same call are not delivered and no exception reaches the caller. The list forms return just the entries before it.

`getLatestHistoryEntryVersion(s)` returns the highest version among the structure's AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY rows (C_ID in [s<<32, (s+1)<<32)), or 0 when the structure has no entries. It reflects the stored history, not the forest's current version (if the latest change was not recorded, the two differ).
`getEarliestHistoryEntryVersionGtEqDate(s, t)` returns the lowest version among the structure's entries with C_TIMESTAMP >= t (inclusive), or 0 when no entry of the structure is that recent.

`getEntryCount(s)` returns the number of AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY rows of the structure; `getEntryCountGtEqDate(s, t)` counts only those with C_TIMESTAMP >= t (inclusive). Both return 0 for a structure without history.

The per-structure methods need a structure ID in 1..2^31-1 and versions >= 0 to build the packed history key: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run), a structure ID of 0 or less (e.g. `getEntryCount(0)`) throws `AssertionError`; with assertions disabled, the key is computed anyway and the result is undetermined (normally no entries / 0).

A database failure in the version and count queries (`getLatestHistoryEntryVersion`, `getEarliestHistoryEntryVersionGtEqDate`, `getEntryCount`, `getEntryCountGtEqDate`) or while streaming entries is thrown as the plugin's unchecked storage exception (a `StructureRuntimeException`), not as a `StructureException`.

`getForestVersion(s, v)` first checks that the current user may VIEW the structure (the structure manager's access check, honouring `StructureAuth` security override). If not, or if the structure does not exist, it throws `StructureException` with error `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for structure s, before validating the version and even when the version is cached.

`getForestVersion(s, v)` returns a `ForestVersion` whose `fullForest` is the structure's whole stored forest as it was right after version v was recorded (rebuilt from the current forest by undoing the entries newer than v, or from a cached nearby version), and whose `entry` is the history entry with version v including all its changes. For v equal to the current forest version, `fullForest` equals the current forest. The forest is not filtered by row or issue visibility and is immutable.

`getForestVersion(s, 0)` returns the forest obtained by undoing every stored entry of the structure (the initial state, normally empty) together with a synthetic entry: structure s, version 0, prev version 0, timestamp 0, null user key, null synchronizer and an empty change list.

`getForestVersion(s, v)` for v greater than the structure's current forest version, or for a v in range that has no AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ENTRY row (an unrecorded or purged version other than 0), throws `StructureException` with error `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`, whose item is the long identity of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-structure-version` with ID (s << 32) | v.

`getForestVersion(s, v)` with a negative v on a structure the user can view: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws `AssertionError` (the packed key needs v >= 0); with assertions disabled the failure is undetermined (the packed key no longer names structure s, so some `StructureException` results). It does not reliably give `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` (as the original does).

In the entry returned by `getForestVersion`, each change's `getAfterFrom()` and `getAfterTo()` lists, when not empty, are extended at the front with all preceding siblings of the stored after-row, taken from the reconstructed forest at that step (old position before the change, new position after it). For example, rows A, B, C under one parent and an ADD of X after C gives an after-to list [A, B, C] instead of [C]. Entries from `getHistoryEntries` keep the stored one-element lists.

Successful `getForestVersion` results are cached by (structure, version) in a size-bounded LRU cache (weight limit 4,194,304 by `ForestVersion.weight`): a repeated call returns the same `ForestVersion` instance without reading the database (the access check still runs each time). Failures are not cached. Clearing the plugin caches (`CachingComponent.clearCaches`) empties it.

If rebuilding a version fails with a `StructureException` (for example a change that cannot be undone on the forest), that exception is thrown unchanged by `getForestVersion`; any other exception during the rebuild is wrapped in a `StructureException` with error `GENERIC_ERROR` and the original as its cause.

`queryActivity(query, limit, consumer)` delivers matching entries newest first: by C_TIMESTAMP descending, ties by packed key (structure, version) descending. A positive `limit` caps the number of entries delivered to the consumer; 0 or a negative value means no limit. Delivery also ends when the consumer returns false (that entry counts as delivered). Entries skipped by the permission or ancestor filters do not count towards the limit.

In `queryActivity`, `HistoryQuery.startId` keeps only entries whose packed key (structureId << 32 | version) is strictly less than it; `minDate`/`maxDate` keep entries with C_TIMESTAMP >= minDate and <= maxDate (both inclusive).

In `queryActivity`, a non-empty `isStructuresSorted` keeps only entries of those structures and `notStructuresSorted` is then ignored; with an empty inclusion list, entries of every structure in `notStructuresSorted` are excluded.

In `queryActivity`, a non-empty `isAuthors` keeps entries whose C_USER_KEY is one of the keys (`notAuthors` then ignored); otherwise a non-empty `notAuthors` keeps entries whose user key is not among them. Under SQL semantics entries with a null user key are dropped by either author filter. At most the first 100 values of an author, issue, project or synchronizer list are used (a warning is logged for more).

In `queryActivity`, `isIssuesSorted` keeps entries indexed in AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_ISSUE with at least one of the issue IDs; otherwise `notIssuesSorted` keeps entries indexed with at least one issue not in the list (entries touching no issue are dropped). `isProjectsSorted`/`notProjectsSorted` do the same with AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_PROJECT. Each entry is delivered once even when several index rows match.

In `queryActivity`, a non-null `HistoryQuery.operations` keeps only entries with at least one change of one of those operations; null means no restriction. If `operations` is an empty set (what the full `HistoryQuery` constructor makes from a null or empty argument), `queryActivity` throws `NullPointerException` (as the original does).

In `queryActivity`, `isSynchronizersSorted` keeps entries whose C_SYNCHRONIZER is one of the IDs, where -2 also admits manual entries (null synchronizer) and -1 admits any synchronizer; a list holding both -2 and -1 is no restriction. `notSynchronizersSorted` is applied as well: plain IDs exclude those synchronizers (and, by SQL semantics, also manual entries), -1 excludes all synchronizer entries, -2 excludes manual ones. When the exclusion list holds -2 together with other IDs, those IDs are not excluded at all: any entry made by a synchronizer passes (as the original does).

Unless `StructureAuth` security is overridden, `queryActivity` skips entries of structures the current user cannot VIEW (checked once per structure per call); an anonymous user without access sees nothing. With security overridden no structure or row filtering is applied.

Unless security is overridden, `queryActivity` filters each change's forest by row visibility for the current user (the `ForestAccessCache` invisible-row set): invisible rows are removed but invisible ancestors of visible rows stay (soft filtering), `getOriginalRows` is narrowed to match the remaining rows, and the paths and after-lists are kept unchanged. A change whose filtered forest is empty is dropped, and an entry left with no changes is skipped. An entry with nothing hidden is passed on unchanged.
`queryActivity` never delivers an entry that has no changes (none stored, or none left after filtering), even when the query has no ancestor conditions.

In `queryActivity`, an entry is kept only if at least one of its changes passes both ancestor conditions. `isAncestors` (if non-empty) passes a change when a row on its from-path or to-path shows one of the given items, or, when an issue or project filter is set, when its forest has more than one row and contains a row of a given item with an issue below it that matches the issue/project filter. `notAncestors` fails a change on the same test. Rows that no longer exist count as not matching.

`queryActivity(query, limit, changesLimit, consumer)` with a positive `changesLimit` loads at most that many changes per entry (in C_ID order) and passes the entry's change count as the second argument of `LimitedHistoryConsumer.consume`: when the limit was reached, the count of all AO_8BAD1B_HISTORY_CHANGE rows of the entry (before permission filtering); otherwise the number of changes loaded. With `changesLimit` <= 0 all changes are loaded and the count is the loaded number. The three-argument form loads all changes.

`addTotalCountAsync(name, value)` adds `value` to an in-memory pending total for `name` (`addTotalCountAsync(name)` adds 1.0); nothing is written at call time. At the next flush the total becomes one AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS row with C_STAT = name, C_USERKEY null and C_VALUE = the sum of all values added since the previous flush (e.g. three calls with 1.0 give one row with 3.0).

`addUniqueUserCountAsync(name)` records the current `StructureAuth` user for `name`; at the next flush one AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS row per distinct user key collected since the previous flush is written (C_USERKEY = the user's key, C_VALUE 0.0). The same user recorded twice in one window gives one row; a user whose key is null is stored as the empty string.

`addUniqueUserCountAsync` does nothing when there is no current user (anonymous). Any recording method given a null, empty or whitespace-only name records nothing and logs a warning. Neither case throws, not even after the plugin stopped.

Within one flush window a statistic name is either a total count or a unique-user statistic, decided by its first recording: a later `addUniqueUserCountAsync` for a name already holding a total (or a total for a name holding users) is ignored with a logged warning. After a flush the name starts fresh.

`addToIntValueDistrAsync(prefix, value, bins...)` adds 1.0 to the total count `<prefix>.<bound>`, where bound is the first given bound (in the given order) that is >= value, written as a decimal integer; when the value is above all bounds the name is `<prefix>.inf`. Example: bins 10, 100 and value 10 gives `prefix.10`, 11 gives `prefix.100`, 500 gives `prefix.inf`. With no bins nothing is recorded.

`addTotalCountAndActiveUserAsync(name)` adds 1.0 to the total `name` and records the current user under the unique-user statistic `activeUser.<name>` (the user part is skipped for an anonymous caller).

After the plugin component has stopped, a recording call that would record something (a non-blank name, and a current user for the unique-user form) throws `StructureStoppedException`. Before the plugin has started, recording works and lazily starts the component's background jobs.

Pending values are flushed by a background job every 600 seconds (first run 600 s after start; interval from dark feature `structure.statisticsManager.pendingJobIntervalSeconds`). All rows of one flush share one C_TIMESTAMP: the time of the most recent recording before the flush. While the plugin's database is locked the flush is skipped and the pending values are kept for the next run. An empty window writes nothing.

The component registers a scheduled job under key `statistics.lastSentTime` that runs when at least 86,400,000 ms (dark feature `almworks.statistics.dev.requestInterval`) have passed since its last run; it deletes all AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS rows with C_TIMESTAMP older than now minus 40 days (3,456,000,000 ms). The job is removed when the component stops.

The replacement never sends usage statistics anywhere: even with the global property `statistics.sendingEnabled` set to true, the daily job only purges old rows. Opting in just stores the property value ('true'/'false'); `statistics.sendingEnabled` reads as false when unset. (The original posted an aggregated report to the vendor; that is out of scope, SPEC.md §1.8.)

`addStatisticSource` registers a `StatisticSource` whose `getStatistics()` map is merged into each statistics report assembled afterwards (after the stored statistics and `dayCount`, later sources overwriting equal names); a source that throws is logged and skipped. The same source added twice is registered twice; `removeStatisticSource` removes one registration and ignores an unknown source. Registrations live in memory only.

The 'enable statistics' offer is shown to a user only when sending is not enabled, the user has not dismissed it (Jira user property `com.almworks.jira.structure.statistics.offerRejected` not true) and at least 3 distinct users are recorded under the `userCount` statistic in AO_8BAD1B_STATISTICS. Dismissing sets that user property to true. The user count is cached and re-read only after a flush that contains `userCount` while the cached answer was 'not enough'.

`addRecords(records)` inserts one AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY row per record in list order: C_LONG_ID = the item identity's long ID, C_TYPE_ID = the item type's ID (registered in AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE if new), C_NEW_NAME/C_NEW_DESCRIPTION/C_NEW_PARAMETERS from the new item, C_OLD_* from the old item (all null when it is null), C_AUTHOR = author key, C_TIMESTAMP, C_CREATE. Parameters are stored as JSON, or null when the map is empty. The records' own IDs are ignored; new auto-increment IDs are assigned.

After `addRecords`, the `ItemTracker` is told about the changed generic items (each item identity once) and then about the new record items (`CoreIdentities.memoChangeHistoryGroup(newId)` for each stored record), and any cached lookup of those record identities is dropped so `getRecord` sees the new row.

If storing a record fails with the plugin's storage exception, `addRecords` logs a warning and returns normally: records before it stay stored, it and all later records are not written, and the item tracker is still notified for the records that were stored. After the component has stopped, `addRecords` throws `StructureStoppedException`.

`getRecord(identity)` returns the record for a long identity of type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo-change-history-group` whose ID is an AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY.ID, with `getId()` = that ID, the item identity rebuilt from C_TYPE_ID and C_LONG_ID, and author, timestamp and create flag from the row. Any other identity (another type, or a string identity) or a missing row gives null. No permission check.

A record read back from storage has `getOldItem()` null whenever C_OLD_NAME is null or blank (old description and parameters are then ignored); otherwise the old item has the stored old name, description and parameters. The new item always has the stored new name, description and parameters (empty map when C_NEW_PARAMETERS is null).

`getRecord` results, including 'not found', are cached per identity (slowly expiring cache, timeout from `structure.genericItemRecord.cache.timeout`); a row changed directly in the database is not seen until the entry expires, `addRecords` creates that record, `removeRecordsForItems` runs, or plugin caches are cleared. A database error while loading throws the plugin's storage exception.

`loadRecords(identities, consumer)` ignores identities that are not memo-change-history-group long identities, passes first the records already cached (in input order, skipping cached 'not found'), then reads the rest from AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY by ID in chunks of 1000 (dark feature `structure.genericItemHistory.chunkSize`), each chunk in C_TIMESTAMP order. IDs with no row are silently skipped; records read this way are not added to the cache.

`loadRecordsForItems(itemIds, consumer)` passes every AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY record whose (C_TYPE_ID, C_LONG_ID) matches one of the given item identities. Identities are grouped by item type (group order unspecified) and read in chunks of 1000, each chunk ordered by C_TIMESTAMP; an item with no history yields nothing. An item type key not yet known is registered in AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE as a side effect.

`removeRecordsForItems(itemIds)` deletes all AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY rows of the given generic items (matched by type and long ID) and then empties the whole record cache, so `getRecord` of a removed record returns null. The item tracker is not notified. An empty collection deletes nothing.

On a single-node server the tracker keeps its journal in memory: it starts at a `DataVersion` with a signature unique to this plugin start and version 1, and each non-null identity passed to `recordChange`/`recordChanges` increases the version by exactly one (an item recorded twice counts twice). Null identities are skipped without changing the version. AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2 is not written.
`getUpdate(v)` with v equal to the current version returns an update with `isEmpty()` true and the current version.

`getUpdate(v)` for a version of the current signature that is behind by n (1 <= n <= 500) recorded changes, all still in the journal, returns an incremental update: `isFull()` and `isEmpty()` false, `getFromVersion()` = v, `getVersion()` = the current version, and `getAffectedItems()` = the set of item identities recorded since v (long and string identities preserved, duplicates collapsed).

`getUpdate(v)` returns a full update (`isFull()` true, no affected items, version = current) when v is null, has another signature (from an earlier plugin start, or `DataVersion.ZERO`), is newer than the current version, is more than 500 changes behind, or reaches back past the 20,000 most recent changes kept in the journal or past a `reset()`.

`reset()` forgets the journal and increases the version by one: any `getUpdate` from a version taken before the reset returns a full update, while `getUpdate` from the version right after the reset is empty until something new is recorded.
`recordChanges(null)` throws `NullPointerException` (only null elements are tolerated). `recordChanges` with an empty iterable changes nothing.

When the plugin started, the tracker registers with the plugin's issue-reindex tracking: after a full Jira reindex or a project reindex completes it calls `reset()` (dark features `structure.memoryBasedItemTracker.fullUpdateByFullReindex` / `...fullUpdateByProjectReindex`, both default true; on Data Center `structure.reindexAwareItemTracker.*`), so clients get a full update. Reindexing individual issues does not reset. On stop it unregisters.
`recordChange`, `recordChanges`, `getUpdate` and `reset` have no lifecycle check: on a single-node server they work before the component starts and after it stops.

On Jira Data Center, changes recorded on a node are visible to `getUpdate` on that node immediately and are also queued and written asynchronously by a background thread to AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2 (C_TYPEID from AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE, C_ITEMID or C_ITEMSID, consecutive C_ID in the node's partition from AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2). Before answering `getUpdate`, a node reads new events of other live nodes (re-checked at most every few minutes through a cache) and records them locally, so they appear on other nodes with a delay.

On Data Center, when a node's queued batch has more than 500 changes, a full update, or would overflow the node's event-ID partition, the node re-initialises its partition instead of writing the events: it gets a new signature in AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2 and deletes its partition's events, and other nodes that notice the new signature reset their tracking (their clients get a full update).

On Data Center (with `structure.delegatingItemTracker.enableReindexMonitor`, default true), an issue change arriving from another node is recorded right away only if this node reindexed that issue within the last 2 seconds; otherwise it is held back until the local reindex of the issue completes, or until 6 seconds pass (checked on the next read), so that consumers do not see an issue change before the local index has it. Changes of other item types and changes recorded locally are not delayed.

The maintenance option `cleanupItemTracker` deletes all rows of AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_EVENTS_V2 and AO_8BAD1B_NODE_SIGNS_V2 (the latter under the event signature cluster lock) and then resets the tracker, so clients get a full update. On a single-node server it does nothing.

The bridge registers its Jira event listener with Jira's `EventPublisher` when the component starts and unregisters it when it stops; Jira events published before start or after stop are not passed to `IssueListener`s. `addListener`, `removeListener`, `reportChanges` and `reportEvent` work regardless of the lifecycle state.

Listeners are called in registration order, synchronously on the reporting thread. `addListener(null)` is ignored; a listener added twice is called twice per event; `removeListener` removes one registration and ignores unknown or null listeners. A listener added or removed during a delivery does not affect that delivery.

An `Exception` thrown by a listener's `onIssueChanged` is logged and the remaining listeners are still called; the caller of `reportEvent`/`reportChanges` (or Jira's publisher) sees no exception. An `Error` (for example `AssertionError`) is not caught: it stops delivery to later listeners and propagates to the caller (as the original does).
When Jira's `ImportUtils.isEnableNotifications()` is false (e.g. during an import), no listener is called, neither for Jira events nor for `reportEvent`/`reportChanges`.

`reportChanges(issueIds, type)` delivers one `IssueChangeEvent` per element of the list, in list order (duplicates delivered twice), each with that issue ID, the given change type and no Jira event (`getJiraEvent()` null). A null list does nothing; an empty list does nothing. A null type throws `NullPointerException` at the first element (even if there are no listeners).
`reportEvent(event)` delivers that same event object to every listener; null is ignored.

A Jira `IssueEvent` becomes an `IssueChangeEvent` carrying the issue's ID and the original event (`getJiraEvent()`), with the type mapped from the Jira event type: created to ISSUE_CREATED, updated ISSUE_UPDATED, assigned ISSUE_ASSIGNED, resolved ISSUE_RESOLVED, closed ISSUE_CLOSED, reopened ISSUE_REOPENED, deleted ISSUE_DELETED, moved ISSUE_MOVED, work started ISSUE_STARTED, work stopped ISSUE_STOPPED, commented COMMENT_CREATED, comment edited and comment deleted COMMENT_UPDATED, work logged WORKLOG_CREATED, worklog updated WORKLOG_UPDATED, worklog deleted WORKLOG_DELETED, generic event GENERIC_EVENT; any other event type ID gives GENERIC_EVENT. An event without an issue, or whose issue has no ID, is dropped with a warning.

An `IssueEventBundle` is unpacked and each contained event handled in order; a `DelegatingJiraIssueEvent` is handled as its `asIssueEvent()`; an `OnCommitIssueEvent` as its wrapped issue event. A Jira `IssueChangedEvent` gives an ISSUE_UPDATED `IssueChangeEvent` for its issue without a Jira event.

A Jira `FieldValuesChangedEvent` gives a GENERIC_EVENT `IssueChangeEvent` for its issue (no Jira event). If it is for a new issue and its modified fields include `issuelinks`, a second identical notification is sent about 1000 ms later (dark feature `structure.issueListener.linkDiscoveryTimeout`; 0 or less disables the second one).
Jira `IssueLinkCreatedEvent`/`IssueLinkDeletedEvent` give a `LinkChangeEvent` of type LINK_CREATED/LINK_DELETED with the link's type ID, source issue ID and destination issue ID.

For a remote issue link event the bridge looks the link up by ID through Jira's `RemoteIssueLinkManager`. If found with an issue ID, it sends an `IssueChangeEvent` for that issue: REMOTE_LINK_CREATED for create (API or UI) events, REMOTE_LINK_REMOVED for delete events, REMOTE_LINK_UPDATED for update events. If not found and the event is an API create event, it sends REMOTE_LINK_CREATED for every issue having a remote link with the event's global ID (lookup failures are logged). Otherwise nothing is sent, so a delete whose link is already gone reports nothing (as the original does).

Jira `IssuePropertySetEvent` and `IssuePropertyDeletedEvent` give an ISSUE_UPDATED `IssueChangeEvent` (no Jira event) for the property's entity ID, only when the property is present and its entity ID is positive.
`getForestSource(null)` throws `StructureException` with error `INVALID_PARAMETER` (message `forest spec is null`); nothing else happens.

For a secured spec, `getForestSource` checks on every call (also when the source is already cached): if the spec has a user key, `UserManager.getUserByKey` must return a user, otherwise it throws a `StructureException` with error code 6008 (an internal error of category NO_PERMISSION, not one of the public `StructureErrors`) for the user identity of that key; a null user key means anonymous. If the spec names a structure, the structure permission of that user (not of the current user) must include VIEW, otherwise `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for that structure (also for a structure that does not exist). A secured query or clipboard spec without a structure needs only the user check.

An unsecured spec is not permission-checked, but when it is first resolved (cache miss) a non-null user key it carries (for example a transformed or query spec) must still name an existing Jira user, otherwise the same user-not-found `StructureException` (code 6008) is thrown. An unsecured structure spec of a structure the user cannot see is resolved without error.

Equal specs give the same `ForestSource` instance while it is cached: a second `getForestSource` with an equal spec returns the identical object without building a new one. Sources are held per node in memory with soft references and expire 30 minutes after last access (specs whose transformations include the module `com.almworks.jira.structure:filter-item` go to a separate cache that expires after 5 minutes). Dark features `structure.forestService.cache.<general|pinned>.timeout` (ms; negative disables expiry), `.maxSize`, `.concurrency` and `.softValues` (default true) tune the two caches. Clipboard specs are never cached by this module: each call asks the clipboard for its source again.
A spec whose query has type `text` and an empty query string is resolved as the same spec with a `jql` query and an empty query string (so both resolve to the same cached source).

A spec with a query of type `jql`, `text` or `cql` resolves to a forest whose only top-level row is a new transient generator (created through `generator-manager`'s `createTransientGenerator`) with parameters {<type>: <query>, "limit": 1000}: module `com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-jql` for jql, `com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-text` for text, `com.almworks.structure.pages:inserter-confluence-pages` for cql. With an empty query the module is `com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-recent-issues` (jql and text) or `com.almworks.structure.pages:inserter-recent-pages` (cql) with the same parameter map. The generator is not checked to be installed.

For any other query type, `getForestSource` uses the `SQuerySkeletonFactory` extension registered for that type: its `createSkeleton(query, builder)` fills the forest. When no factory is registered for the type it throws `StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` with message `'<type>' sQuery type is not supported`.

For a non-skeleton spec (query, transformed, titled or structure spec) the returned source is a generating source: when its forest is requested it runs the generators found in the underlying forest (the query, sub-structure and transformation generators described for each kind, or the structure's own generators). The fixed skeleton forests built for query, transformed and titled specs are immutable; an action applied directly to such a skeleton throws `StructureException` `UNSUPPORTED_FOREST_SOURCE_OPERATION`.

An unsecured structure spec (no version, not transformed, no title) resolves to the structure's stored forest source from `structure-manager` without a permission check; when the structure does not exist this throws `StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`. A skeleton spec returns that stored source itself (so `apply` on it changes the structure); a non-skeleton spec wraps it in a generating source that also runs the structure's generators.

A structure spec with a version resolves, with security overridden (`StructureAuth.sudo`), to the forest of that version from `HistoryService.getForestVersion(structureId, version)`, as an immutable source whose version number is the history entry's version; errors from the history service propagate as `StructureException`. Such a source cannot be changed.

A transformed spec is resolved to a forest of two top-level generator rows, both transient generators created through `generator-manager`: first a sub-structure inserter (module `com.almworks.jira.structure:inserter-substructure`) whose parameters hold the spec without its last transformation in REST form, its user key and whether it is secured, row id 0 and reuse-rows true; then a generator with the last transformation's module key and parameters. Each transformation therefore stacks on the source of the spec before it. This happens before the secured check of the build, so secured transformed specs are built this way too.

A spec with the title flag (and no transformations) is resolved to a forest whose single top-level row shows the structure itself (item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-structure` with the structure id, semantics 1) with one child: a transient sub-structure inserter generator for the same spec without the title flag.

A secured, untransformed spec resolves to a secured source wrapping the source of the unsecured spec (which is resolved, and cached, at the same time). Each time the secured source fetches the underlying forest it re-runs the user and VIEW checks; if they now fail (user deleted, permission revoked) it shows an empty forest instead of throwing.

Resolving a non-skeleton spec that names a structure records the use of that structure: the structure property `lastPolledMillis` is set to the current epoch milliseconds, at most once per 2 hours per structure on each node. Skeleton specs do not record use.

When building a source fails with something other than a `StructureException` (for example a spec with neither structure, query nor clipboard, which fails with `IllegalArgumentException` inside), `getForestSource` throws `StructureException` `GENERIC_ERROR` with that failure as cause. A `StructureException` raised while building propagates unchanged.

`getDisplayName` of a structure spec (also a secured, versioned or skeleton one) returns the structure's name as `StructureManager.getStructure(id, VIEW)` gives it for the current user. When that fails (no such structure, or the current user may not view it) the error is logged and the result is the text of i18n key `s.common.structure` (English `Structure`) in the current user's language.

`getDisplayName` returns, in the current user's language: for null the text of `s.common.structure` (English `Structure`); for a query spec `s.common.query` (`Query`); for a clipboard spec `s.common.clipboard` (`Clipboard`); for a secured spec the name of its unsecured form; for a transformed spec the name of its untransformed form followed by ` (+)` (added once only: a name already ending in ` (+)` is not extended). It never throws.

Clearing the caches for a user (the `CachingComponent` call) drops every cached source whose spec carries that user key, and every source of a structure owned by that user, so the next `getForestSource` builds them anew; clearing all caches drops every cached source. Dropped generating sources have their running generation cancelled.
When the plugin stops, every generation running for a cached spec is cancelled (with interruption).

`createRow(itemId, semantics)` inserts a row into `AO_8BAD1B_ROW`: `C_ITEM_TYPE` is the `item-type-registry` id of the item's type key (registered if new), `C_ITEM_LONG_ID` the long id (0 for string-id items), `C_ITEM_STRING_ID` the string id (NULL for long-id items), `C_SEMANTICS` the semantics. It returns `ID * 2` (positive, even). The row is visible to `getRow`, `scanRows` and `findRows` on this node right after the call. A null item throws `NullPointerException`; a database id that overflowed to a non-positive number gives `StructureRuntimeException` `Row ID overflow detected: <pk>`.

`getRow(id, access)` returns a row with the stored item identity and semantics for an existing id: odd positive ids are transient rows (in memory), even positive ids persistent rows. For 0, negative ids, and ids that were never created or were lost on restart (transient) it throws `MissingRowException` for that id. The item is resolved lazily through `item-resolver` according to the access mode.

The plugin's `scanRows(rows, sorted, access, missing, predicate)` does nothing for null rows. Otherwise it first checks all ids: a 0 or negative id is added to the missing collector, or with a null collector throws `MissingRowException` before any row is visited. It then visits all transient (odd) rows in the given order, and after them the persistent (even) rows: in the given order when `sorted` is true, or sorted ascending (duplicates kept) when `sorted` is false. Missing rows go to the collector or throw `MissingRowException`.

In `scanRows`, a predicate returning false stops the visit only within the current group: when it returns false for a transient row, the remaining transient rows are skipped but the persistent rows are still all passed to the predicate (as the original does). A false for a persistent row ends the scan.

`findRows(itemId, predicate)` reports first the persistent rows of the item (rows of `AO_8BAD1B_ROW` whose long id, or string id, and item type match; order as returned by the database), then the transient rows of the item, newest first, until the predicate returns false. A null item reports nothing. Issues are looked up by issue id, other items by their identity; results are cached and refreshed when a row for that item is created on this node. Looking up an item whose type key is not yet registered registers it in `AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE`.

When the database lookup for the persistent rows fails, `findRows` logs it and reports no persistent rows, but it still goes on to report the transient rows (the empty answer may be cached for a while). No exception reaches the caller.

`createMapper(forest).mapRow(id)` returns -1 for -1; the id itself when it is a row of the forest; 0 when it is not in the forest and is not a transient id (persistent, 0 or negative). For a transient id not in the forest it reads the row: missing row gives 0; a row without a creator (creator 0) gives 0; when the row's creator id is a row of the forest it returns that transient id (even though the row itself is not in the forest); otherwise it continues with the row's original id (0 gives 0).

`mapRow` follows at most 100 original-id steps (dark feature `structure.rowmapper.maxjumps`) and returns 0 when the limit is reached; after 15 steps (`structure.rowmapper.normaljumps`) it also watches for an id seen before and returns 0 on such a cycle. Both cases are logged.

`map(rows)` maps each id with `mapRow`. When every id maps to itself it returns `Mapping.identical(rows)` with the same list. Otherwise the mapped list keeps unchanged ids, replaces changed ids by their mapped id (and the map holds requested -> mapped for them), and leaves out ids that map to 0, so it can be shorter than the requested list; the result is `Mapping.mapped(rows, mappedList, map)`.

`createGenerator(moduleKey, params, owner)` inserts a row into `AO_8BAD1B_GENERATOR` with `C_MODULE_KEY` the trimmed key, `C_PARAMETERS` the parameters as a JSON object (NULL when the map is null or empty) and `C_OWNING_STRUCTURE` the owner (NULL allowed), and returns `C_ID * 2`. It does not notify the item tracker. A null or blank key throws `IllegalArgumentException` before anything is stored; after the plugin has stopped it throws `IllegalStateException`.

`createTransientGenerator(moduleKey, params)` keeps the generator in memory only and returns odd ids 1, 3, 5, ... in creation order (starting again at 1 after a restart); nothing is written to the database and the owning structure is null. The key is trimmed and a blank key throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

`getGenerator(id)` returns a `GeneratorSpec` for an existing id: for a persistent id (positive even) the stored key, parameters read back from the JSON (null column gives an empty map) and owner; for a transient id (positive odd) the spec as created. For an id that does not exist it returns null (no exception). For 0 or a negative id: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) it throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled it returns null. Persistent results are cached and the cache is refreshed after create, update and delete on this node.

`updateGenerator(id, key, params, owner)` on a persistent id overwrites all three columns (null params store NULL, null owner clears `C_OWNING_STRUCTURE`) and then calls `ItemTracker.recordChange` with the generator's identity (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator`, id). An id that is not positive and even throws `StructureException` `INVALID_PARAMETER` with the localized message `Generator <id> is not editable.` (checked before the key); a persistent id with no row throws `StructureException` `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for the generator identity with message `Generator <id> does not exist.` and records no change. A blank key on a persistent id throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

`deleteGenerator(id)` on a persistent id deletes its row and, only if a row was deleted, records a change of the generator identity with `ItemTracker`; on a transient id it removes it from memory without notifying. Deleting a missing id does nothing and throws nothing. For 0 or a negative id: with assertions enabled it throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled it does nothing. `getGenerator` returns null afterwards.
No method checks permissions or whether the module key belongs to an installed generator; any non-blank key is stored as given (trimmed).

`resolveItem(id, cls)` finds the item type module registered for the identity's type key and calls its `StructureItemType.accessItem(id)`. It returns the object cast to `cls` when it is non-null, is an instance of `cls`, and either security is overridden (`StructureAuth`) or the type's `isVisible(object, user)` is true for the current `StructureAuth` user; otherwise null. A null identity or an unknown type key gives null. A null `cls` throws `NullPointerException`, even for a null identity.
Exceptions (and linkage errors) thrown by the item type while loading or checking visibility are logged and give null; `resolveItem` and `resolveUnchecked` never throw for them.

`resolveUnchecked(id)` returns whatever the item type's `accessItem` returns, without class or visibility check and without calling `isVisible`; null for a null identity, an unknown type or a failure.

`resolveItems` and `resolveItemsUnchecked` do nothing for an empty collection, and a null collection gives `NullPointerException`. A collection of exactly one identity is resolved as by `resolveItem` / `resolveUnchecked` and is always reported to the consumer, with null when not resolved (also for a null element or an unknown type). A null class or consumer gives `NullPointerException` before anything else.

With two or more identities, they are grouped by type key. For a type that is a `BulkAccessibleItemType`, `accessItems` is called once with the type's identities (an unmodifiable set), each object it reports is passed on (after the class and visibility check; null if it fails), and afterwards each identity it did not report is passed with null. For other types `accessItem` is called per identity. Identities of an unknown type are not reported at all. Order of reporting is not defined.

In the bulk case, an exception thrown by an item type is logged and ends that type only: identities of that type not reported before the failure are not reported at all (also not with null), while other types are still resolved.

When a collection of two or more identities contains the same identity twice (for example a `List`), `resolveItems` and `resolveItemsUnchecked` throw `IllegalStateException` (duplicate key) before reporting anything (as the original does); a null element among two or more gives `NullPointerException`.
The visibility check uses the user of the current `StructureAuth` context, read once per call (bulk calls use the same user for all items); with security overridden `isVisible` is not called.

`getOrCreateTypeId(key)` trims the key and returns the `ID` of the `AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE` row whose `C_KEY` equals it, inserting a new row when there is none. Repeated calls with the same key (also with surrounding spaces) return the same id, which never changes. A null, empty or whitespace-only key throws `IllegalArgumentException` (message `argument cannot be null or blank`).

On the first lookup that misses the in-memory mapping, all rows of `AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE` are loaded at once; afterwards known keys and ids are answered from memory without database access. Cleared caches are reloaded the same way on the next miss.

When inserting a new key fails (a unique-constraint conflict because another thread or node inserted it, or another database error), it tries again: up to 5 attempts, each first reading the key and inserting only if absent, waiting 50, 100, 200 and 400 ms between attempts. If several rows hold the key, the first one found is used. After 5 failed attempts, or when the plugin stops while waiting, it throws a `StructureRuntimeException` (`cannot record a new item type <key> in 5 attempts`); an interrupt also gives a `StructureRuntimeException` and keeps the thread's interrupt flag set.

`getTypeKey(id)` returns the `C_KEY` of the row with that `ID`. For an id with no row it throws `ItemTypeNotFoundException` (message `item type <id> was not found`); this is not remembered, so a later registration with that id is found. A row with a null key gives a `StructureRuntimeException`.

When the answer is not already in memory, both methods require not being inside a database transaction: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) they throw `AssertionError` when called inside one; with assertions disabled they proceed.
After the plugin has stopped, `getTypeKey` and `getOrCreateTypeId` throw `IllegalStateException` (not a `StructureRuntimeException`), even for cached entries.

The first call of any `StructureViewManager` method on a node checks the global property `createdDefaultViews` (in `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY`).
