If it is not true, it takes a cluster-wide lock, checks again, creates the default views and the global default view settings with security overridden, and then sets `createdDefaultViews` to true. Once true, nothing is created again, even if the default views are later deleted. The check is made once per node lifetime.

If creating the default views fails with a `StructureException`, the method that triggered it throws a `StructureRuntimeException` (`cannot create default views`) and the property stays unset, so the next call tries again; views created before the failure are kept and reused by name.

The default views, in creation order, are named with the Jira default locale texts of `s.w.view.default.<details|basic|planning|tracking|triage|entry|gadget>.name` (English: `Issue Details`, `Basic view`, `Planning`, `Tracking`, `Triage`, `Entry`, `Gadget View`) with the matching `.description` texts. When a view with the same name already exists, it is reused (the one with the lowest id among same-named views) and not changed. New ones have no owner and the rules: anyone VIEW, then ADMIN for each Jira group holding the global ADMINISTER permission.

Columns of the new default views (field columns by Jira field id; `icons` is the type-and-priority icons column; `progress` the progress column; `main` the summary column; `sum` an aggregate): Issue Details: issuekey, main. Basic view: issuekey, main, progress, icons. Planning: issuekey, icons, main, duedate, fixVersions, assignee, scrollable column mode (2), and with time tracking on: timeoriginalestimate (unless time tracking is in legacy mode), timeestimate, sum of timeestimate. Tracking: issuekey, icons, main, progress, status, duedate, assignee, mode 2, and with time tracking on: timeestimate, sum of timeestimate, timespent, sum of timespent. Triage: issuekey, main, issuetype, priority, assignee, components, versions, labels. Entry: issuekey, main, description, environment, and with time tracking on: timeoriginalestimate, sum of timeoriginalestimate. Gadget View: issuekey, main, progress, assignee.

Initialization stores global default view settings (row `C_STRUCTURE_ID` 0 of `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW`) listing, in this order: Basic view (on all menus, default on structure board, issue page and project tab), Issue Details (menus: structure board and project tab), Planning (menus: board, issue page, project tab), Tracking (all menus), Triage and Entry (menus: board, issue page, project tab), Gadget View (menu: gadget only). The licence write check is skipped for this.

`getView(id, level)` returns the view when it exists and, unless security is overridden, the current user may use the plugin and their view permission includes `level`. A null `level` asks for no minimum, so any plugin user gets the view, even with NONE access to it (as the original does). Otherwise it throws `StructureException` `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` for that id: also for null, 0, negative ids, ids outside the int range, missing rows and rows whose `C_DATA` is empty or not valid JSON.

`getViewPermission(id, user)` gives NONE when the view does not exist; otherwise ADMIN for a Jira administrator (unless administrators' view access is turned off by configuration), NONE for a user who may not use the plugin, ADMIN for the owner, else the level from the view's rules (NONE when no rule applies). It does not look at the current user or at security override.

`isAccessible(id, level)` for an existing view is true with security overridden, otherwise true when the current user may use the plugin and their view permission includes `level` (null: always). For a missing view it is true only when the current user may use the plugin and `level` is null or NONE.

`getViews(level)` returns every stored view that `getView(id, level)` would return, sorted by name with the current user's collator; with a null level that is every view for any plugin user. Views that cannot be read are skipped. If the list of view ids cannot be loaded it returns an empty list. The id list is cached without expiry and refreshed when views are created or deleted through this manager.

`createView()` returns an unsaved view with id 0, empty name and description, no owner, no rules and an empty specification; nothing is stored until `saveChanges()`. Saving it requires the right to create views (`VIEW_CREATION_DENIED` otherwise), sets the current user as owner unless security is overridden or the user is anonymous, requires a non-blank name and a specification (`INVALID_PARAMETER`), checks sharing when rules are non-empty, inserts a row into `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW` with the JSON in `C_DATA`, and the view then has the new row id.

Saving a loaded view with no pending changes does nothing. Otherwise it applies the changes to the stored JSON (read anew from `C_DATA`), requires EDIT on the view, or ADMIN when name, description, owner or rules differ from the stored ones (`VIEW_EDIT_DENIED` / `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED`, `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` without access or when the row is gone), validates changed rules, and rewrites `C_DATA`. An invalid result (blank name) gives `INVALID_PARAMETER`.

`deleteView(id)` requires ADMIN on the view: a missing view or one the current user cannot access at all gives `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` (even with security overridden for a missing view), lower access `VIEW_ADMIN_DENIED`. It deletes the `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW` row and all `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE` rows of the view; `AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_TO_VIEW` settings that mention the view are left as they are. Unlike `getView`, it does not check that the user may use the plugin. The licence write check passes in the replacement (no licensing).

`getViewSettings(structureId)` requires that the current user may view the structure (`StructureException` `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` otherwise, also for null). It returns the settings parsed from the structure's `C_VIEW_SETTINGS`; undefined settings (`isDefined()` false) when there is no row, the column is NULL or it cannot be parsed; `ViewSettings.EMPTY_SETTINGS` on storage errors. Results are cached.

`setViewSettings(structureId, settings)` requires ADMIN on the structure (`STRUCTURE_ADMIN_DENIED` with VIEW, `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` without; with security overridden the structure must still exist). Without a row it inserts one with version 0 (nothing is stored when the settings are null); with a row it writes the new JSON (or NULL for null settings) and version + 1 only if the version is still the one just read. After a successful write it inserts `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE` rows (structure, view, new version) for each associated positive view id and deletes that structure's rows with older versions. If another writer changed the row in between (or won the insert), the call returns normally and the change is lost (as the original does).

`getDefaultViewSettings()` returns the settings stored for structure id 0 without any access check (undefined settings when none; `EMPTY_SETTINGS` on storage errors). `setDefaultViewSettings(settings)` requires a Jira administrator unless security is overridden (`StructureException` `JIRA_ADMIN_DENIED`) and stores the settings in row 0 the same way as structure settings, without touching `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE`.

`getMenuItems(structureId, page)` returns an empty list when the structure is given and the current user may not view it. It uses the structure's settings if defined, else the global default (a null structure id always uses the default). It lists, in settings order, every associated view that is on the menu of `page` and that the current user can VIEW (missing views skipped); the first one that is default for the page is placed first and flagged preferred; later views that are also default for the page keep their place and are also flagged preferred.

`getAssociatedStructures(viewId)` requires that the current user has some access to the view (unless security is overridden): a missing view, or NONE access (which includes users who may not use the plugin), gives `VIEW_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE`; a missing view gives it even with security overridden and returns, without duplicates and sorted by name with the current user's collator, the structures listed for the view in `AO_8BAD1B_VIEW_TO_STRUCTURE` that the current user may view. If the list cannot be loaded it returns an empty list.

`makeDefaultForStructure(viewId, structureId, page)` checks ADMIN on the structure, then VIEW on the view (errors as for `setViewSettings` and `getAssociatedStructures`). It starts from the structure's settings, or the global default when the structure has none. If the view is already the default for the page, nothing is written. If the view is not associated, it is added at the front with menu and default pages both just `page`. If it is associated, `page` is removed from every view's default pages and added to this view's default and menu pages. The result is saved with `setViewSettings` (so it becomes the structure's own settings).

When `makeDefaultForStructure` changes a view that is already associated and appears on all menus (menu pages unset), its menu pages become only `page`, so it disappears from the menus of the other pages (as the original does).

The replacement does no licence checking (SPEC.md §1.1): `deleteView`, `setViewSettings`, `setDefaultViewSettings`, `makeDefaultForStructure` and saving a view never fail, and are never made read-only, on licence grounds.

createItem(typeKey, item) inserts one AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM row: C_NAME = the item's name, C_OWNING_STRUCTURE = its owning structure as given (null allowed; not checked to exist), C_DESCRIPTION = its description, C_PARAMETERS = the parameter map as compact JSON (null when the map is empty, never `{}`), C_TYPE_ID = the AO_8BAD1B_ITEM_TYPE id of the type key (created if the key has none yet). It returns the long identity `<typeKey>/<new row ID>`; a following getItem of that identity returns an item equal to the one given.

createItem throws a StructureException with error CREATE_ITEM_FAILED, message `Generic item type '<typeKey>' is not supported`, and stores nothing when the type key is not the complete key of an installed structure item type module whose item type is a GenericItemType (for example `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder` or an unknown key). The two built-in generic types `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task` are accepted. No licence, app-access, anonymous-user or permission check is made.

After a successful createItem one AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY row is appended for the new item: C_CREATE true, C_OLD_NAME/C_OLD_DESCRIPTION/C_OLD_PARAMETERS null, C_NEW_* = the stored name, description and parameters, C_LONG_ID = the new ID, C_TYPE_ID = the item's type id, C_AUTHOR = the user key of the current StructureAuth user (null when there is none), C_TIMESTAMP = the current server time in epoch ms. ItemTracker is then told that the new item identity changed. A failure to write the history row is only logged; createItem still succeeds.

getItem(identity) returns the stored item (name, owning structure, description, parameters parsed from the JSON; no parameters gives an empty map) when a row with that ID exists and its type key equals the identity's type key. It returns null for a string identity, for an ID with no row, for an ID outside the 32-bit int range, and for a type mismatch (a memo's ID asked for as `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task/<id>` gives null). No permission check: items owned by structures the current user cannot see are returned too.

getItem results, including 'not found', are kept in a per-node cache keyed by numeric ID (expiry configured by the dark feature `structure.genericItem.cache.timeout`); createItem, updateItem and deleteItem drop the entry, so a read after a change through this manager sees the change. A load failure of the cache surfaces as an unchecked storage exception, not as null.

loadItems(identities, consumer) reads the items straight from the database (not the cache), in chunks of at most 1000 IDs (dark feature `structure.genericItemManager.chunkSize`), and calls the consumer once with (identity, item) for every identity in the set whose row exists with the same type key; missing IDs and type mismatches are skipped silently and the order of calls is not defined. An empty set makes no call. A string identity in the set throws UnsupportedOperationException before anything is loaded.

updateItem(identity, item) overwrites C_NAME, C_OWNING_STRUCTURE, C_DESCRIPTION and C_PARAMETERS of the existing row with the given item's values (an owning structure of null clears it; an empty parameter map stores null). It then appends an AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY row with C_CREATE false, the old name/description/parameters as they were before and the new ones, C_AUTHOR = the current StructureAuth user key (or null) and the current time, drops the cache entry and tells ItemTracker the identity changed. The history row is written even when the new data equals the old.

updateItem with a string identity throws a StructureException with error INVALID_PARAMETER (message `<identity> is not a long ID`). With a long identity whose ID has no row, or whose row has another type key, it throws a StructureException with error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE for that item (message `Cannot find item #<identity> or it is not accessible`) and changes nothing. No permission check is made.

deleteItem(identity) hard-deletes the AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM row when a row with that ID and the same type key exists, drops the cache entry and tells ItemTracker the identity changed. It writes no history row and leaves the item's existing AO_8BAD1B_GENERIC_ITEM_HISTORY rows and any forest rows pointing to it in place. A missing ID or a type mismatch does nothing and does not throw; a string identity throws a StructureException with error INVALID_PARAMETER.

getOwnedItem(identity, structureId, copyIfSame) on an existing item with no owning structure updates that item in place so its owning structure becomes structureId, keeps name, description and parameters, writes no history row (ItemTracker is still told it changed) and returns the same identity, whatever copyIfSame is.

getOwnedItem on an existing item owned by another structure, or owned by structureId itself when copyIfSame is true, creates a new item of the same type with the same name, description and parameters and owning structure structureId (exactly as createItem does, with a create history row and an ItemTracker notification) and returns the new identity; the original item is left unchanged. Owned by structureId with copyIfSame false returns the identity unchanged and stores nothing.
getOwnedItem returns the given identity unchanged and stores nothing for a string identity and for a long identity whose item does not exist (or exists with another type key).

isVisible(item, user) is true for an item with a null owning structure without consulting StructureManager; otherwise it asks StructureManager.getStructurePermission(owningStructure, user) and is true exactly when that level includes PermissionLevel.VIEW (a null user is passed through as anonymous; a structure that does not exist or the user cannot see gives false).

After the plugin has stopped, createItem, getItem, loadItems, updateItem, deleteItem and getOwnedItem throw StructureStoppedException (unchecked). Before the first start they work normally. isVisible does not check the lifecycle state.

getItem(identity) returns a failed result with a StructureException of error STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED (message `User has no access to Structure app`), no item and no identity, when StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser() is false; the manager is not asked. getItem makes no licence check.

getItem returns a failed result with a StructureException of error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE for the identity (message `<identity> is not found`) and no item when GenericItemManager.getItem gives null (missing ID, type mismatch or a string identity).

When the item exists but GenericItemManager.isVisible(item, current StructureAuth user) is false, getItem returns a failed result whose exception has error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (message `<identity> is not accessible`) and which still carries the item in getGenericItem(). When visible, the result is valid, carries the item and has a null getItemId().

validateCreate(typeKey, item) fails, in this order of checks: when the app may not be used by the current user (StructurePluginHelper.isStructureAvailableToCurrentUser() false) with error STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED; when there is no current StructureAuth user (anonymous) with error CREATE_ITEM_FAILED and message `<typeKey> item can't be created by anonymous user`. Otherwise it is valid. The licence check always passes in the replacement (no Marketplace licensing; the original would report LICENSE_PROBLEM first when unlicensed). The type key and the item's owning structure are not checked. The result returns the given type key and item unchanged and has an empty error collection.

create(validation) with a valid validation calls GenericItemManager.createItem(type key, item) and returns a valid result whose getItemId() is the new identity (no item). A StructureException from the manager (for example CREATE_ITEM_FAILED for an unsupported type key) is returned as the result's exception instead of being thrown. With an invalid validation nothing is created and the result carries the validation's error collection and exception.

validateUpdate(identity, newItem) fails with error STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED when the current user may not use the app; with error INVALID_PARAMETER (message `<identity> is not a long ID`) for a string identity; with error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE (message `<identity> is not found or not accessible`) when GenericItemManager.getItem gives null. The licence check always passes in the replacement. Failed and valid results both return the given identity and new item.

When the existing item has an owning structure, validateUpdate also fails with error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE when GenericItemManager.isVisible(existing, current user) is false, and with error ITEM_EDIT_DENIED for the item (i18n key `s.item.edit.error.no-edit-perm` with the structure id as argument) when StructureManager.isAccessible(owningStructure, PermissionLevel.EDIT) is false for the current user. An existing item with no owning structure passes with app access alone. The new item's owning structure is never checked, so an update may move the item to any structure.

update(validation) with a valid validation calls GenericItemManager.updateItem and returns a valid result with neither item nor identity; a StructureException from the manager (for example the item was deleted after validation, ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE) is returned as the result's exception. An invalid validation is passed on: errors and exception copied, nothing stored.

validateDelete(identity) fails with error STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED without app access; INVALID_PARAMETER for a string identity; ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE when the item does not exist or GenericItemManager.isVisible(item, current user) is false; and ITEM_EDIT_DENIED (i18n key `s.item.edit.error.no-edit-perm`, the owning structure id as argument) when StructureManager.isAccessible(owningStructure, PermissionLevel.EDIT) is false. For an item with no owning structure that last check is made with a null structure id, which is never accessible, so deleting an unowned item through this service always fails with ITEM_EDIT_DENIED (as the original does). The licence check always passes in the replacement.

delete(validation) with a valid validation calls GenericItemManager.deleteItem and returns a valid result with neither item nor identity; a StructureException from the manager is returned as the result's exception. An invalid validation is passed on with its errors and exception and nothing is deleted.

None of the service methods throws StructureException; every business failure is reported through the returned result (isValid() false with getException() set and an empty error collection). Unchecked exceptions from the manager, such as StructureStoppedException after the plugin stopped, are not caught.

isFavorite(structureId, user) is true exactly when AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES has a row with C_USER_KEY = the user's key and C_STRUCTURE_ID = structureId. It is false for a null structure id, a null user or a user whose key is null, without reading storage. Whether the structure exists or is visible is not checked. Each user's set of favourite ids is cached (dark feature `structure.favorites.cache.timeout`) and refreshed by setFavorite.

setFavorite(structureId, user, true) deletes every AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES row for that (user key, structure id) pair and inserts exactly one new row, so repeating it leaves one row; setFavorite(..., false) deletes the pair's rows. A null structure id, null user or user with a null key stores nothing. No permission or existence check is made. Afterwards the user's cached favourites and the structure's cached popularity are refreshed, even when the storage call failed.

getPopularity(structureId) returns the number of AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES rows with that C_STRUCTURE_ID (0 when there are none, for a structure that does not exist, and for a null id); setFavorite changes it immediately for that structure. If the count cannot be loaded it returns 0 and logs a warning. The count is cached per structure (same expiry setting as the favourites).

getFavorites(user, includeArchived) returns the given user's favourite structures that StructureManager.getStructure(id, PermissionLevel.VIEW) can load for the current StructureAuth user (not the given user); ids of structures that are missing or not viewable by the current user are silently skipped. Archived structures are left out unless includeArchived is true. The list is sorted with StructurePluginHelper.getStructureComparator(given user) (by name in that user's locale). A null user gives an empty list. getFavorites(user) is getFavorites(user, false).

getAllFavorites() reads every AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES row and returns a new map from user key to a LongArray of that user's favourite structure ids, sorted ascending with duplicates removed; the map iterates in ascending user-key order. Ids of structures that no longer exist and keys of users that no longer exist are included; no access check is made. With no rows it returns an empty map.

sortByPopularity(structures, user) reorders the given list in place: higher popularity first; equal popularity ordered by StructurePluginHelper.getStructureComparator(user); null elements last. A null or empty list is left alone. The list must allow element replacement (an unmodifiable list throws UnsupportedOperationException).

filterByPopularity(structures, min, max) returns a new list with the structures, in their original order, whose popularity p satisfies min <= p <= max (min greater than max gives an empty list). A null list gives an empty list. A null element counts as popularity Integer.MIN_VALUE, so it is kept only when min is Integer.MIN_VALUE.

After the plugin has stopped, isFavorite, setFavorite, getPopularity, getFavorites, sortByPopularity and filterByPopularity throw StructureStoppedException. getAllFavorites does not check the lifecycle state.

The maintenance option `cleanupFavorites` deletes every AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES row whose user key Jira's UserManager does not resolve to an existing user, or whose structure id is not among all structures (StructureManager.getAllStructures(PermissionLevel.ADMIN, true), archived included); other rows stay. When anything was deleted all cached favourites and popularity counts are dropped.

When Jira erases a user's personal data, the module reports favourite structures as data to delete only when getFavorites(user, true) is non-empty (count = its size, description key `s.anonymize.favorite-structures.description`), and on deletion removes every AO_8BAD1B_FAVORITES row with that user's key, drops that user's cached favourites and all popularity counts, and reports success with no errors.

CachingComponent.clearUserCaches(user) drops the cached favourites of the current StructureAuth user, not of the given user (nothing when there is no current user) (as the original does); clearCaches() drops all cached favourites and popularity counts.

createFolder(folder) inserts one AO_8BAD1B_FOLDER row with C_NAME = the folder's name and C_OWNING_STRUCTURE = its owning structure (null allowed; not checked to exist), returns the new auto-increment ID, and tells ItemTracker that `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder/<id>` changed. getFolder(id) right after returns a folder with that name and owner. No permission check.

getFolder(id) returns a new Folder with the stored name and owning structure, or null when no row has that ID (including 0, negative IDs and IDs outside the 32-bit int range). Results, including 'not found', are cached per ID (dark feature `structure.folder.cache.timeout`) and refreshed by this manager's create, update and delete; a cache load failure throws an unchecked storage exception.

updateFolder(id, folder) overwrites C_NAME and C_OWNING_STRUCTURE of the row with the given folder's values (a null owner clears it), refreshes the cache and tells ItemTracker the folder identity changed. When no row has that ID it throws a StructureException with error ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE for item `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-folder/<id>` (message `Cannot find folder #<id> or it is not accessible`) and changes nothing.

deleteFolder(id) deletes the row and, only when a row was deleted, refreshes the cache and tells ItemTracker the folder identity changed. A missing ID does nothing and does not throw. Forest rows showing the folder are not touched.
After the plugin has stopped, createFolder, getFolder, updateFolder and deleteFolder throw StructureStoppedException.

getMemo(id) looks up `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo/<id>` through GenericItemManager.getItem and returns null when that gives null (no such ID, or the ID belongs to a planning task); otherwise a Memo snapshot of the item as loaded. No permission or app-access check.

getMemos(ids) returns one Memo per ID in the order of the collection, leaving out IDs with no memo; a duplicated ID gives a duplicated entry; an empty collection gives an empty list. Each ID is looked up separately. No permission check. A null collection throws NullPointerException.

A Memo's getSummary() is the item's name and getDescription() its description; getAssignee(), getDueDate(), getOriginalEstimate(), getRemainingEstimate() and getTimeSpent() come from the item parameters' `fields` map under the keys `assignee` (Jira user key), `duedate` (`yyyy-MM-dd`), `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate` and `timespent` (decimal milliseconds). A missing key, a non-string value or a value that cannot be parsed reads as null.

Memos allow exactly these fields: summary, description, assignee, duedate, timeoriginalestimate, timeestimate and timespent; none is required. A stored value is also checked against the field's own rules on read (for example an assignee that is not a valid option); a value that fails reads as null instead of throwing.

getUpdateBuilder(id) returns a new, empty builder for `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-memo/<id>` without reading or checking anything; setters only record values (setting a field twice keeps the last value) and return the same builder.
MemoUpdateBuilder.setSummary throws IllegalArgumentException (message `Cannot set summary to an empty value`) for null, empty or whitespace-only text, at once and without recording anything.

update() first reads the memo through GenericItemService.getItem as the current user and throws that result's StructureException: STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED without app access, ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE when the memo does not exist or is owned by a structure the user cannot view. It then validates the recorded values; finally it runs GenericItemService.validateUpdate and update and throws their exception, e.g. ITEM_EDIT_DENIED when the user lacks EDIT on the owning structure. A memo with no owning structure may be changed by any user with app access. Nothing is stored when any step fails.

When a recorded value fails validation (a field not editable for memos, or a value the field rejects) update() throws a StructureException with error UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED carrying the field's localized error message, and stores nothing. This check comes before the EDIT permission check.

A successful update() keeps every field not set, writes summary to the item name and description to the item description (null clears it), and puts the other fields into the parameters' `fields` map as strings (assignee as the user key, due date as `yyyy-MM-dd`, durations as the decimal number of milliseconds given); setting a field to null removes its key, and the `fields` key disappears when the map becomes empty. Other parameter keys (such as `color`, `iconClass`) are preserved. The change goes through GenericItemManager.updateItem, so a history row is written and ItemTracker notified.

When the memo had neither `timeoriginalestimate` nor `timeestimate` stored and an update leaves exactly one of the two non-blank, the other is set to the same value: setOriginalEstimate(3600000) on such a memo makes getRemainingEstimate() 3600000 too. Once either estimate is stored, the two are independent.

getPlanningTask(id) looks up `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task/<id>` through GenericItemManager.getItem and returns null when that gives null (no such ID, or the ID belongs to a memo); otherwise a PlanningTask snapshot. No permission or app-access check.

getPlanningTasks(ids) returns one PlanningTask per ID in the order of the collection, leaving out IDs with no planning task; a duplicated ID gives a duplicated entry; never null. A null collection throws NullPointerException.

PlanningTask getters return the summary from the item name, the description from the item description and every other field from the parameters' `fields` map under its Jira field id (`environment`, `assignee`, `reporter`, `priority`, `issuetype`, `project`, `duedate`, `timeoriginalestimate`, `timeestimate`, `labels`, `versions`, `fixVersions`, `components`, `customfield_<n>`). Each value is then checked against the Jira field configuration for the task's stored project and issue type as seen by the current StructureAuth user: a field hidden there, or a value not valid there (e.g. a version of another project), reads as null. Values that cannot be parsed read as null.

The custom-field getters of PlanningTask (getTextCustomFieldValue, getDateTimeCustomFieldValue, getNumberCustomFieldValue, getDateCustomFieldValue, getLabelsCustomFieldValue, getProjectCustomFieldValue, getSingleVersionCustomFieldValue, getMultiVersionCustomFieldValue, getSingleUserCustomFieldValue) throw IllegalArgumentException `Field <field name> is unsupported` when the plugin does not support that custom field for generic items, and `Field <field name> is of wrong type` when the field's kind does not match the getter (text accepts single-line and multi-line text). getSprint() returns null when Jira has no sprint custom field.

getUpdateBuilder(id) returns a new, empty builder for `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-planning-task/<id>` without checking that the task exists; setters record values (the last value per field wins) and return the same builder; nothing is written until update().
PlanningTaskUpdateBuilder.setSummary throws IllegalArgumentException (message `Cannot set summary to an empty value`) for null, empty or whitespace-only text.

The custom-field setters of PlanningTaskUpdateBuilder throw IllegalArgumentException at once, `Field <field name> is unsupported` for a custom field the plugin does not support for generic items and `Field <field name> is of wrong type` when the field's kind does not match the setter; a null value is accepted and clears the field on update.

setSprint throws StructureRuntimeException `Sprint changing is not enabled` when Jira has no sprint custom field or the agile sprint services are not available. Otherwise null records 'no sprint', and a non-null sprint is looked up by its id in the agile application; when none is found it throws IllegalArgumentException `Cannot find a sprint with id <id>`.

update() throws StructureException: STRUCTURE_PLUGIN_ACCESS_DENIED without app access; ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE when the task does not exist or its owning structure is not visible to the current user; UPDATE_ITEM_FAILED with the localized field error when a recorded value is not editable, hidden or invalid in the Jira field configuration for the task's project and issue type after the change (so changing the project re-checks the other values against the new project), or is empty for a field that configuration requires; ITEM_EDIT_DENIED when the user lacks EDIT on the owning structure. Only the fields being set are validated. Nothing is stored on failure.

A successful update() keeps fields not set, stores summary as the item name and description as the item description, puts the other fields into the parameters' `fields` map as strings under their Jira field id (null removes the key; the `fields` key disappears when empty), applies the same estimate fill-in as memos (when neither estimate was stored and only one is now set, the other gets the same value), and stores through GenericItemManager.updateItem (history row, ItemTracker notification).

Each property is one AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_PROPERTY row: C_COMPOSITE_KEY = `<structureId>:<key>` (key not trimmed, e.g. `12:showDescription`), C_STRUCTURE_ID = the structure id, C_VALUE = the value. setValue with a non-blank value creates the row or overwrites its value; setValue with null, empty or whitespace-only text deletes the row (no error when there is none). The structure is not checked to exist and no permission check is made.

getString(structureId, key, default) returns the stored value of `<structureId>:<key>`, or default when there is no row or its value is null; a load failure also gives default (warning logged). The value is cached per composite key with a moderate expiry (dark feature `structure.properties.cache.timeout`); setValue and removeAllProperties refresh the affected entries on this node, so a read after a write through this service sees the write.

getString and setValue check with Java assertions only that the structure id is >= 0 and the key has at most 170 characters: with assertions enabled (as the tests run) a negative id or a 171-character key throws AssertionError; with them disabled the call goes on with that composite key.

getAllKeys(structureId) reads the database directly (not the cache) and returns a new modifiable set of the plain keys (without the `<id>:` prefix) of all rows with that C_STRUCTURE_ID; empty when there are none.
removeAllProperties(structureId) deletes every row with that C_STRUCTURE_ID and drops their cached values, so getString afterwards returns the default; other structures' properties stay.

The maintenance option `cleanupStructureProperties` deletes every AO_8BAD1B_STRUCTURE_PROPERTY row whose C_STRUCTURE_ID is not among all existing structures (StructureManager.getAllStructures(PermissionLevel.ADMIN, true), archived included) and then drops the whole cache.

set(key, value) stores the value in AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY: C_KEY = the key with leading and trailing whitespace removed, C_VALUE = the value exactly as given (whitespace-only values are stored). An existing row's value is overwritten; a new key creates a row. A null or empty value deletes the row instead (no error when there is none). remove(key) is the same as set(key, null). No permission check.

set(String, String), set(String, boolean), set(String, long) and remove throw IllegalArgumentException (message `argument cannot be null or blank`) for a null, empty or whitespace-only key and store nothing.
The getters do not trim the key: after set(" a", "x") the value is stored under `a`, getString("a", null) returns `x` and getString(" a", null) returns null (as the original does).
getString(key, default) returns the stored value, or default when there is no row or the row's value is null; a load failure returns default and logs a warning.

getBoolean(key, default) is true when the stored value is exactly `true`, false for any other stored value (including `TRUE` or ` true`), default when none is stored. getLong(key, default) parses the stored value as a decimal long and returns default when none is stored or it does not parse (e.g. `1.5`, ` 5`). set(key, boolean) stores `true`/`false`; set(key, long) stores the decimal text (e.g. `-7`).

Values are cached per key without expiry (also 'not set'); every set and remove refreshes the entry for its trimmed key, even when the storage call failed. A row changed by other means is not seen until invalidate(key) for that key or clearCaches() drops the cached value; invalidate changes no stored data.

The `lifecycle` component's `LifecycleAware.onStart()` starts the plugin's controlled components on a new daemon thread named `starter:com.almworks.jira.structure` and returns at once without waiting for them. A second `onStart()` without an `onStop()` in between does nothing except log a warning about an out-of-order call; likewise `onStop()` when not started does nothing except log the warning. After `onStop()`, a later `onStart()` starts everything again.

The components started by `lifecycle` are the modules of the enabled plugin `com.almworks.jira.structure` that are enabled by default and take part in the plugin's controlled start/stop (if the plugin is not enabled in Jira's `PluginAccessor`, the list is empty and nothing is started). They are started one by one in a fixed order (sorted by implementation class name) on the starter thread, and stopped in exactly the reverse order of the ones that were actually started. Each component is started at most once per start cycle.

Before starting any component, the starter thread waits until every selected module is enabled in Jira, re-checking at least once per second (dark feature `structure.lifecycle.modulesEnablementMinWaitMs`, default 1000) for at most 60 seconds in total (`structure.lifecycle.modulesEnablementTotalWaitMs`, default 60000). If modules are still disabled after that, the start is treated as fatal: an error naming the disabled modules' complete keys is logged and the plugin `com.almworks.jira.structure` is disabled through Jira's plugin controller (asynchronously, at most once per lifecycle instance). With dark feature `structure.lifecycle.startAnywayWithDisabledModules` true it logs an error instead and starts only the enabled ones. If `onStop()` is called during the wait, no component is started.

An exception or linkage error thrown by one component's start (or stop) is logged as an error (start) or warning (stop) naming the component, and the remaining components are still started (or stopped); the start sequence is not aborted. An interruption of the starter thread ends the start sequence. The start sequence also stops early, with a warning, when the plugin is no longer enabled in Jira or `onStop()` has been called; components after that point are not started.

After all components have been started, `lifecycle` logs at WARN level a banner framed by lines of `+` characters saying `Structure Plugin <version> is started, instance: <id>`, where `<id>` is two lowercase hex numbers joined by a dot (the epoch second when this component was created, and the epoch second when its class was loaded). It then enables the throttled clearing of all plugin caches, registers itself once with Jira's `EventPublisher` (a repeated start does not register twice), and from then on reports the plugin as running.

Retracted (product owner, 2026-10-28: the replacement has no licence checking, so its start banner carries no licence summary). The original's start banner carried a summary of its licence: serial, type, expiry and licensee.

`onStop()` first stops a start that is still in progress: it interrupts the starter thread and waits up to 5 seconds for it (dark feature `structure.lifecycle.threadShutdownWaitMs`, default 5000). Then, before stopping components, it marks the plugin as not running, disables cache clearing (later requests to clear plugin caches do nothing), removes leaked thread-local state of the bundled XML and JSON libraries, clears Jira's Velocity template cache, unregisters from `EventPublisher` and logs a WARN banner `Structure Plugin is shutting down, instance: <id>`. It then stops the started components in reverse order and logs a warning listing any component that was not stopped cleanly.

While subscribed, when Jira publishes `ComponentManagerShutdownEvent` the `lifecycle` component immediately marks the plugin as not running and disables cache clearing, without stopping any component itself (that happens later through `onStop()`). The plugin counts as running only while this flag is set and the lifecycle has been started and has not shut the plugin down after a fatal start error.

`Pinger.ping(subject, period)` with a null subject throws `NullPointerException`; with a period below 500 ms throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `cannot ping faster than once in 500ms`; 500 is accepted. These checks happen only while the service is not stopped: after the `pinger` component has been stopped, `ping` returns silently for any arguments, including null or a too-short period, and registers nothing.

A registered `Pinger.Pingable` is not called immediately: its first call comes on the first round at least `period` ms after registration, and later calls at least `period` ms after the previous call (rounds are about 166 ms apart, so periods are rounded up to the round grid). The argument is the `System.nanoTime()` value taken at the start of that round, the same for every callback called in the round. Within one round, due callbacks are called one after another in registration order on the same thread.

A callback whose `ping` returns false is removed and never called again by that registration. A callback that throws any `Exception` or `LinkageError` is also removed, and a warning `error when pinging <callback>` is logged; other callbacks keep running. A callback returning true stays registered.

Registering the same callback object twice (even with the same period) creates two independent registrations, each called on its own schedule. `stopPinging(subject)` removes every registration whose callback is the same object (identity, not `equals`); an equal but different object is not removed. It never throws: an unknown or null subject does nothing, a call after the service has stopped does nothing, and any internal error is logged.

The `pinger` runs callbacks on one daemon thread of priority 4 named `structure-pinger #<n>`, where n counts the threads started (1 for the first). Registrations made before the component has started are kept, and the thread is created when the component starts (or on the first registration after start) provided at least one registration exists; no thread runs while nothing was ever registered. When no registration has existed for 2 minutes the thread exits (logged `structure-pinger exiting by idle timeout`); a later `ping` starts a new thread with the next number. If the thread ends for any other reason while registrations remain, a new thread is started right away.

When the `pinger` component is stopped it wakes the thread, removes all registrations, waits up to 200 ms for the thread to finish and interrupts it if it is still alive; no callback is called after that. The stop is final for this component instance: later `ping` and `stopPinging` calls are ignored. A component stopped before it was ever started also ends up stopped.

`dependency-watcher` watches exactly two plugins: `com.pyxis.greenhopper.jira` (Jira Software), whose package `com.atlassian.greenhopper.api.rank` must be exported at version 9.4.0 or higher, and `com.atlassian.servicedesk` (Jira Service Management), whose package `com.atlassian.servicedesk.api` must be exported at version 5.1.0 or higher. Events about any other plugin never cause a refresh.

`onStart()` registers the watcher with Jira's `PluginEventManager` and then runs a startup check over all currently enabled plugins; `onStop()` unregisters it. While registered, each `PluginEvent` (with a non-null plugin) about a watched plugin is checked the same way; null events are ignored.

If Jira application property `com.almworks.jira.structure.system.refreshedOnStart` is `true` when `onStart()` runs, the startup check is skipped entirely and the property is set to `false` (this is the start that follows a refresh caused by a startup check). Otherwise the check runs; when it triggers a refresh, the property is set to `true` before the refresh is launched. Refreshes caused by plugin events do not touch the property.

A refresh is needed for a watched plugin when it is uninstalled (`PluginUninstalledEvent`), or when all of these hold: both it and the Structure plugin are OSGi plugins with bundles (not uninstalled), its bundle is resolved, starting, stopping or active, Structure's bundle is starting or active, the watched package is exported by that plugin's bundle at the required version or higher, and Structure's bundle is not among the package's importers. For a `PluginEnabledEvent` the importer test is treated as failed, so enabling a watched plugin that exports a good enough package always triggers a refresh. A missing export, a lower version, the export coming from another bundle or a null importer list means no refresh. Any error during the check is logged as a warning and means no refresh.

A watcher instance launches at most one refresh: once one has been launched, further checks return no refresh. The refresh runs on its own daemon thread: it logs a WARN line naming the plugin and the cause (the event's simple class name, or `startup check`), disables every enabled plugin that depends (mandatorily or optionally) on `com.almworks.jira.structure`, disables Structure, refreshes Structure's OSGi bundle packages (only if the bundle is resolved), re-enables Structure when that is possible, and then re-enables the dependent plugins. If the refresh thread could not be launched, the watcher allows a later refresh. If the Structure plugin was not an OSGi plugin when the watcher was created, it never refreshes.
The `upgrade.001` SAL upgrade task reports build number 1 (`getBuildNumber()`), plugin key `com.almworks.jira.structure` (`getPluginKey()`) and short description `upgrade prepare`.
`doUpgrade()` of `upgrade.001` returns null (no messages), changes no data and calls no Jira service.

When the `upgrade.001` component is created and JVM system property `structure.upgrade.reset` is `true` (as read by `Boolean.getBoolean`, so case-insensitive `true` only), it removes key `com.almworks.jira.structure:build` from the SAL global plugin settings (`PluginSettingsFactory.createGlobalSettings()`), so SAL re-runs all upgrade tasks. With the property absent or any other value, the settings are not touched.

`cloud-data-migrator` reports `com.almworks.jira.structure` as both its server app key and its cloud app key. Its Forge app id is the UUID in dark feature `structure.forge.migration.appId`, default `94d5de1a-112d-4549-bd03-5f910d5fd27b` (an unparsable value makes `getForgeAppId` throw `IllegalArgumentException`), and its Forge environment name is dark feature `structure.forge.migration.environment`, default `production`.

`getDataAccessScopes()` returns exactly these eight `AccessScope` values: `APP_DATA_PII`, `APP_DATA_UGC`, `APP_DATA_OTHER`, `PRODUCT_DATA_PII`, `PRODUCT_DATA_UGC`, `PRODUCT_DATA_OTHER`, `MIGRATION_TRACING_IDENTITY`, `MIGRATION_TRACING_PRODUCT`.

On a migration start (Connect `onStartAppMigration(gateway, transferId, details)` or Forge `onStartAppMigration(gateway, details)`), the migrator asks `migration-configuration-manager` for the `AO_8BAD1B_MIGRATION_CONFIG` row whose `C_NAME` equals `details.getName()`. If none exists, all structures and all views are migrated. If one exists with status `DRAFT` or `RUNNING`, the migration is abandoned at once: nothing is uploaded, no status changes, and only a warning is logged. A configuration with an empty structure list also means all structures and views.

With a configuration listing structures, the migrator, with security overridden, reads each listed structure's view settings from the view manager; a structure whose view settings cannot be read (a `StructureException`, for example it no longer exists) is left out and logged as `structure #<id> does not exist`. The backed-up views are the views associated with the default view settings plus those associated with each remaining structure (plus, on the Forge path, views referenced by exported gadgets). If no listed structure remains, the migration is skipped with a log line: nothing is uploaded and the configuration status is not changed.

When a matching configuration is used, its row is updated in `AO_8BAD1B_MIGRATION_CONFIG` as follows (only `C_STATUS` and `C_RUN_AT` change): if its status is not already `READY` it is first set to `READY` with `C_RUN_AT` null; then `RUNNING` with `C_RUN_AT` null; at the end `DONE` with `C_RUN_AT` = current epoch ms on success, or `FAILED` with `C_RUN_AT` = current epoch ms if any `Exception` occurred during the export (the exception is logged, not rethrown). A failure to update the row is only logged. Without a matching configuration no row is written.

The migrated data is a backup made through `StructureBackupManager.backup()` restricted to the chosen structures and views (null for all), without structure history, generic-item history, application configuration and perspectives, but with favourites and saved columns. Extension providers are limited to the configuration's extension keys (with no configuration, all providers; with an empty key set, none). The zip holds the entry `backup.xml` first and then `meta.json`.

`meta.json` (UTF-8) is `{"configs":[...],"selectedConfig":<name or null>}`, where `configs` lists every migration configuration as `{"name":...,"status":...,"structures":[ids]}`. It is computed after the selected configuration has been set to `READY` and before it is set to `RUNNING`, so the selected configuration appears with status `READY`.

The zip is streamed into app-data objects created through the gateway's `createAppData(label)` with labels `structure_backup_0`, `structure_backup_1`, … Each object receives exactly the chunk size in bytes and is closed before the next is created, except the last, which holds the remainder; a new object is only created when more bytes follow, so there is never an empty trailing chunk. The chunk size is dark feature `structure.connect.migration.maxFileSize` (default 1073741824) on the Connect path and `structure.forge.migration.maxFileSize` (default 16777216) on the Forge path.

After the zip is complete, the migrator creates one more app-data object labelled `structure_backup_table_of_contents` containing the UTF-8 JSON `{"count":N,"sequence":["structure_backup_0",...]}` listing the chunk labels in order, and closes it. Only then is the run counted as successful.

On the Connect path dashboard gadgets are never included: the backup has no `gadgets` section and extension providers receive `includeDashboardGadgets` = false. On the Forge path gadgets are included: `dashboard-gadget-data-exporter` exports all Structure gadgets (no structure restriction) or those of the chosen structures, the backup gets a `gadgets` section, providers receive `includeDashboardGadgets` = true, and the numeric `viewId` and `canvas-viewId` preferences of exported gadgets are added to the backed-up views when the views are restricted.

On the Forge path the migrator calls the gateway's `completeExport()` once after the export attempt, whether it succeeded or failed. It is not called when the migration is abandoned early (configuration `DRAFT`/`RUNNING`, or no listed structure remains) (as the original does). The Connect path has no completion call.

`AppSupportStoreReader.isLicenseBlocked(serial)` returns false for every serial, null included. The replacement does no licence checking (SPEC.md §1.1): it keeps no list of blocked serials and reads no stored data to answer, so a property such as `appSupport.blockedSerials` left behind by the original has no effect.

`isLicenseBlocked` never writes to the plugin's stores: calling it any number of times creates, changes or removes no `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY` row (in particular `appSupport.blockedSerials` is left as it is) and makes no network call.

Each call of `StructureBackupManager.backup()` returns a new `BackupOperation` and each call of `restore()` a new `RestoreOperation`; two calls never return the same object. Neither the manager nor the operations check the current user's permissions: an anonymous caller or one without Jira admin rights can back up or restore everything.

`BackupOperation.setFile(null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`null file`); a relative path throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`cannot use relative files`); an absolute path is accepted and the same operation is returned.

`getFinalFile()` before `backup()` returns the configured file, with `.zip` (if `setUseZip(true)`) or `.xml` appended when the file name contains no dot at all; a name with any dot is kept as is (`a.b` stays `a.b` even with zip). With no file set it throws `IllegalStateException`. After a successful `backup()` it returns the file actually written.

`backup()` with no file set throws `IllegalStateException`. Otherwise it creates the missing parent directories; if they cannot be created, or the parent exists but is not a directory, it throws `IOException` and writes nothing. It writes plain XML, or with `setUseZip(true)` a zip with one entry named after the file: a name ending in `.zip` (any case) has that suffix replaced by `.xml`, any other name gets `.xml` appended (`b.dat` gives entry `b.dat.xml`). It returns the same operation.

If writing the backup file fails, the partly written file is deleted and the error propagates: XML writer errors as `IOException` wrapping the cause, I/O errors and `StructureException` unchanged, database errors unchanged, and an exception thrown by an extension provider's `StructureBackupProvider.backup` as an unchecked exception whose cause is the provider's exception. `getFinalFile()` then still reports the target file, not a written one.

`backupToStream(null)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` (`output stream cannot be null`). Otherwise it clears any configured file (so `getFinalFile()` afterwards throws `IllegalStateException`), writes the backup to the stream (plain XML, or with zip a zip whose single entry is `backup.xml`, finished but not closed) and returns the same operation; the stream itself is never closed and is not cleaned up on failure.

A fresh `BackupOperation` backs up all structures and all views, global properties and application configuration, perspectives, favourites, saved columns, generic-item history and every installed extension provider, but not structure history, and writes plain XML (no zip). The document is UTF-8 with root `structure-backup` version `5.0` and a `meta` section whose `by` element holds the user key of `StructureAuth.getUser()` or `system` when that is anonymous.

The backup reads structures (including archived ones) and views with security overridden, so a backup made by a user who cannot see some structures or views still contains them. Structures are written in ascending id order.

`setBackupStructureIds(ids)` (copied; null = all) restricts structures, their forests and manual adjustments, synchronizers, histories, favourites and view associations to those ids. A user's favourites are written only if that user has at least one favourite among the selected structures, and then only the selected ones. The view association of the default (structure id 0) is always kept. The id set is also passed to every extension provider (null when all structures are backed up).

`setBackupViewIds(ids)` (copied; null = all) writes only views with those ids; the `views` element is still present (possibly empty). With `setBackupSavedColumns(false)` the saved-column section is omitted and every column of each written view's specification has its saved-column reference removed from its parameters.

With `setBackupAppConfiguration(false)` the sections `properties`, `configuration`, `attributeSettings` and `darkFeatures` are left out. When included, `properties` holds every row of `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY` except `maintenance.scheduled.nextRunTime`, and `darkFeatures` holds every dark-feature key whose application-property value is non-empty.

`setBackupHistory(true)` adds a `histories` section with the history of each backed-up structure whose forest version is above 0 (structures at version 0 contribute nothing). `setBackupPerspectives(false)` omits the `perspectives` section; when included only valid perspectives are written. `setBackupFavorites(false)` omits `favorites`. `setBackupGenericItemHistory(false)` omits `genericItemHistory`; when included it holds the history records of the generic items written in the backed-up forests.

An installed synchronizer whose owner user key no longer resolves to a Jira user is left out of the backup silently; the others are written with owner key, owner user name, module key, autosync flag and parameters.

`setBackupExtensions(null)` (default) includes every installed `StructureBackupProvider`, an empty set includes none (and no `extensions` element), and a set includes only providers whose declaring plugin key is in it. When no provider is installed there is no `extensions` element. Each included provider gets an `extension` element with attributes `key` (plugin key) and `version` (that plugin's version) and its three-argument `backup` is called with parameter `includeDashboardGadgets` = false for backups made through the public API. Elements the provider left open are closed for it, with a warning.

On a fresh `RestoreOperation`, `restore()`, `checkBackupFile()`, `setRestoreHistory`, `getStructureNames()`, `getErrorsContainer()` and `getProgressGauge()` all throw `NullPointerException` until `setFile` is called. `setFile` reads nothing and does not check that the file exists; it selects everything, including history, and returns the same operation. Calling it again starts over with a fresh, empty problem list and progress.

The restore file type is chosen by name, ignoring case. A `.xml` file is read as plain XML. A `.zip` file must be a zip with an entry, otherwise `IOException` `zip file is empty or corrupt`. Any other name is read as a zip if it opens as one with an entry, else as plain XML. A zip with more than one entry gives `IOException` `too many files in the zip file`. A file that does not exist gives `FileNotFoundException`.

`checkBackupFile()` changes no data and returns the same operation when the first element is `structure-backup` with `version` `3.0`, `3.3` or `5.0`, without reading further. It throws `IOException` (wrapping the XML error) when there is no root element, when the root is `structure` (format too old), when the root has another name, when `version` is missing, or when the version is any other value such as `2.3` or `4.0`.

`restore()` first checks the root element and then reads the whole document once to confirm it is well-formed XML; any failure in this pass throws `IOException` and leaves all existing plugin data and caches untouched. Only then does it drop and recreate the plugin's user-data tables (all existing structures, views and other plugin data are gone), clear plugin caches on all cluster nodes, and read the file a second time to write the backup's contents. An XML error found in the second pass throws `IOException` with the data left partly restored.

For the duration of `restore()` the plugin's storage is locked: the `AO_8BAD1B_BOOTSTRAP` row has `C_IS_LOCKED` true and `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureLocked()` returns true; the lock is released when `restore()` ends, normally or with an exception. If the storage is already locked, `restore()` fails at once with an unchecked exception that is not a `StructureException`, and nothing is read or changed.

Once the data-writing pass of `restore()` has begun, plugin caches are cleared again on all cluster nodes and the users' structure clipboard is emptied at the end, even when the restore fails or is cancelled. A problem during this clean-up is logged, not thrown.

If cancellation is requested through `getProgressGauge()`, `restore()` stops at the next check and returns normally without an exception, with the restore incomplete. If cancellation was requested before `restore()` was called, it returns without touching any data. After a successful restore the gauge reports completion.

After `setFile`, `setRestoreHistory(false)` makes `restore()` skip the backup's `histories` section, so restored structures have no history entries; the default (true) restores them. Other sections are unaffected.

Restore writes every global property found in the backup's `properties` section to `AO_8BAD1B_PROPERTY`. When the backup has a `darkFeatures` section, each listed key is set as a Jira application property, and every dark-feature key currently set in the application properties but absent from that section is cleared; a failure there is only logged. Without the section, application properties are left as they are.

Owners and permission subjects of structures and views that refer to users, projects or project roles missing on this instance are restored unchanged (same user key or id), not dropped. A warning is recorded: for a structure in `ErrorsContainer.getStructureOtherProblems()` under its id, for a view in `getOtherProblems()`.

If one structure cannot be written during restore (a `StructureException`), that structure is deleted again, a message starting `Failed to restore structure: ` is recorded under its id in `getStructureOtherProblems()`, and the restore goes on with the other structures. A view that fails is recorded in `getOtherProblems()` with a message starting `Failed to restore view `, and the rest continue.

Restored synchronizers keep their backed-up ids and are re-enabled for autosync when the backup says autosync was enabled. A synchronizer whose module is not installed is not restored: `getInvalidSynchronizerMessages()` maps its id to `Failed to get plugin module <module key>`, and `getInvalidStructureSynchronizers()` lists its id under its structure id. Install or enable failures are recorded the same way, with their own message.

For each `extension` element in the backup whose `key` matches an installed `StructureBackupProvider`'s plugin key, restore calls that provider's `restore` with a reader on the element and a reporter whose messages go to `getOtherProblems()`. Sections without an installed provider are skipped silently. If the provider throws, `Error occurred while restoring '<key>' extension` (with the cause) is recorded in `getOtherProblems()`, the rest of that section is skipped, and the restore continues.

`getStructureNames()` is empty before `restore()` and afterwards maps each backed-up structure id read so far to its name (structures with an empty name are left out). `getErrorsContainer()` and `getProgressGauge()` return the same objects for the whole life of the operation after `setFile`.

The manager has exactly these executor IDs: `user` (3 threads), `indexing` (2), `system` (1), and `generator`, `attribute` and `effector`, each sized by the Jira application property or JVM system property `structure.jobManager.generatorThreads`, `structure.jobManager.attributeThreads` and `structure.jobManager.effectorThreads` respectively (default: the larger of 4 and the number of processors + 1; a configured value below 1 counts as 1). Each pool queues extra work without limit (it never rejects because it is busy); its threads are daemon threads that end after being idle for `structure.jobManager.thread.timeout` seconds (default 600).

`execute(job, id)` and `execute(callable, id)` with an executor ID that is not one of the seven pools (including null) throw `StructureJobException` whose message contains `illegal executor id` followed by the ID; no job is registered and no ID is used up. (The decompiled source hides this throw: the pool lookup fails with this checked exception, not with `NullPointerException`.) For `execute(job, id)` the null-job and not-PENDING checks and the started check come first.

`enqueue(job)`: a null job throws `NullPointerException`; a job whose `getState()` is not PENDING throws `StructureJobException`; after the plugin stopped it throws `StructureJobException` (message ends with `is stopped`). When the queue already holds `structure.jobManager.queueCapacity` jobs (default 1,000) it throws `StructureJobException` (message contains `job queue is full`); in that case the job has nevertheless been registered under a new ID, so `getJob` of the next ID returns it although it never runs (as the original does).

Before the plugin has started the manager, `enqueue` and `schedule` already accept jobs (they are refused only once the manager is stopped); the jobs wait and run after start, when the queue thread is created. `execute` in all three forms instead requires the manager to be started: before start and after stop it throws `StructureJobException` (message contains `is not started yet or already stopped`).

Enqueued jobs run one at a time on a single background thread, in the order they were enqueued. During each run Jira's logged-in user (`JiraAuthenticationContext.setLoggedInUser`) is set to the job's `getUser()` and reset to null afterwards. An exception thrown by the job is logged and the queue moves on to the next job; nothing is rethrown to the submitter.

A job passed to `execute(job[, id])` runs on a thread of that pool with Jira's logged-in user set to the job's `getUser()` for the duration of `job()` and reset to null afterwards. Any `Exception` (including `InterruptedException`) or `LinkageError` thrown by the job is logged and swallowed, so the job's `Future.get()` returns null normally even when the job failed; other `Error`s are rethrown, so `Future.get()` then throws `ExecutionException`.

Every accepted job (whatever the method) gets the next value of one counter that starts at 1, so IDs are positive and strictly increasing for the plugin's lifetime. On start the manager schedules one recurring maintenance job of its own (no user, every 5 minutes), which takes the next ID at that moment: when nothing was submitted before start it gets ID 1, a client's first job gets ID 2, and `getJob(1)` returns that internal job.

`schedule(initial, interval, job)` checks the job like `enqueue`. The job is due `initial` milliseconds after the call; later runs are due `interval` milliseconds after the previous run finished, and `interval <= 0` means a single run. Before each repeat the manager calls the job's `reset()` (an exception from it is logged and the job is still rescheduled). Due jobs are moved to the single queue and run there like enqueued jobs, but only when the queue thread finds the queue empty for one poll period (3 seconds, property `almworks.singleThreadJobManager.dev.queuePollTimeout`), so a busy queue delays them; a due job that does not fit into a full queue stays scheduled.

`getJob(id)` returns the job object registered under the ID (queued, scheduled, running or finished but not yet cleaned up), and null for a null or unknown ID, a cancelled job, or one removed by cleanup. There is no permission check.

`cancel(id)` unregisters the job (later `getJob` returns null), removes it from the queue and the schedule so it does not run (again), and for a job started with `execute` cancels its future with interruption. A job currently running on the queue thread is not interrupted; it completes but is not rescheduled. A null or unknown ID is ignored, and any caller may cancel any job.

`getFuture(id)` returns the job's `Future` only for jobs started with one of the `execute` methods and only when the job's user key equals `StructureAuth.getUserKey()` of the caller (a job with a null user is visible only to a caller with no user). It returns null for a null or unknown ID, for enqueued or scheduled jobs, and for any other caller.

`execute(callable, id)` records the calling thread's `StructureAuth` context (user and security override) at submission and runs the callable on the pool under that context (`AuthContext.sudo`); Jira's logged-in user is not changed for it. `getJob` returns a job whose `getUser()` is the recorded user. `getFuture(id).get()` returns the callable's result, or throws `ExecutionException` carrying the callable's exception (which is not logged). There is no PENDING check; the manager must be started.

Every 5 minutes the manager unregisters jobs whose state is FINISHED and that finished more than `structure.jobManager.cleanJobsTimeout` minutes ago (default 720), or `structure.jobManager.shortJobsTimeout` minutes (default 3) for callables. A job whose state never becomes FINISHED (a custom `StructureJob`, or a repeating scheduled job, which is reset to PENDING) stays registered.

When the plugin stops, the queue thread is told to stop, the queue, the schedule and the job registry are emptied (every `getJob` returns null afterwards) and all pools are shut down with interruption of running jobs. Afterwards `enqueue`/`schedule` throw `StructureJobException` (`is stopped`) and `execute` throws `StructureJobException` (`not started yet or already stopped`). A stopped manager is never started again, even if start is requested later.

If a queued job throws `InterruptedException` or Jira's `DataAccessException`, the queue thread ends and a replacement is started about 3 seconds later (property `almworks.singleThreadJobManager.dev.reincarnationTimeout`); jobs still in the queue are kept and run on the new thread. The queue thread is also replaced after running for 10 minutes (property `structure.jobManager.jobsThreadTTL`, milliseconds). No replacement is started once the manager is stopped.

When a pool refuses a job submitted with `execute` (it was shut down), the call throws `StructureJobException` whose cause is the `RejectedExecutionException`; for `execute(job, id)` the job stays registered under the ID it was given.

On plugin start (or, if not yet started, on the first `addJob` or `getLastRunTime` call) the manager schedules one recurring check through the `StructureJobManager` (`schedule`, with no user), first after one interval and then every interval; the interval is 60,000 ms, configurable through `almworks.scheduledJobs.dev.checkInterval`. If the job manager refuses, an error is logged and no checks happen.

A periodic check does nothing while `StructurePluginHelper.isStructureLocked()` returns true. During a check the registered jobs are visited one by one, and the visit stops as soon as the manager is stopped.

For each registered job that is not still running, a check reads the last run time stored through `PropertyService` under `sjm.<key>` (a long; missing or unparsable counts as 0) and calls `shouldRun(lastRunTime)`. If it returns true, the manager tries Jira's cluster lock named `com.almworks.structure..sjm.<key>` without waiting; if the lock is held elsewhere the job is skipped this round. Holding the lock it invalidates the property cache for that key, reads the value again and asks `shouldRun` again; if still true it submits the job to the `system` executor of the job manager and, when the submission succeeded, stores the current time in milliseconds (taken just before submitting) under `sjm.<key>`. The lock is released right after submission, not held while the job runs.

A job that has been submitted is not checked or submitted again until its `run()` returns (normally or with an exception, which the job manager logs); after that it is eligible on the next check. Because the `system` pool has one thread, all scheduled jobs (and other system work) run one after another, and a job waiting in that pool already counts as running.

An `Exception` or `LinkageError` thrown by `ScheduledJob.shouldRun` is treated as "do not run" (logged as a warning the first time for that registration, at debug level afterwards); it never stops the check of other jobs.

`addJob(key, job)` registers the job under the key in this node's memory, replacing any job registered under that key (a warning is logged; a running instance of the replaced job is not cancelled). Nothing runs at once: the first run is decided by a later periodic check. After the plugin stopped it throws `StructureStoppedException`.

`forceRun(key)` for a registered key first deletes the stored last run time (`sjm.<key>` is set to null) and then, in the calling thread, does the same due check as the periodic one: if the job is not running, `shouldRun(0)` returns true and the cluster lock can be taken, the job is submitted at once and the new time stored. If the job is running, the stored time is still cleared but nothing is submitted. For an unknown key nothing happens (the property is untouched). It does not check whether the plugin stopped.

`removeJob(key)` unregisters the job and, if a run of it was submitted and has not finished, cancels it through `StructureJobManager.cancel` (interrupting it). The stored `sjm.<key>` value is kept. It does nothing for an unknown key and nothing at all after the plugin stopped.

`getLastRunTime(key)` returns the value stored under `sjm.<key>` parsed as a long, or 0 when there is none or it is not a number; it works for keys that are not registered. It reads through the property service's cache without invalidating it. After the plugin stopped it throws `StructureStoppedException`.
When the plugin stops, every registered job with a run in progress is cancelled through the job manager, all registrations are dropped and the periodic check job is cancelled.

`createNew(user, params)` inserts one row into `AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE` with `C_STATUS` 0, `C_TIMESTAMP` the current time in milliseconds, `C_PARAMETERS` the parameters as JSON (null when params is null), `C_MANAGING_USER` the user's key (null for a null user or an empty key), `C_ACTIVITY` null, `C_PERCENT_COMPLETE` -1 and `C_CANCELLED` false, and returns a handle whose `getId()` is the new row's `ID`. The handle reports status `PENDING`, percent -1, null activity and not cancelled. A serialization failure of the parameters throws `StructureRuntimeException`.

`getInfo`, `getFeedback` and `getUIController` return null for a null ID and for an ID with no row. If the row exists but cannot be read (for example `C_PARAMETERS` or `C_ACTIVITY` holds invalid JSON) they also return null and log an error. Otherwise each returns a full process handle for that ID (the same kind of object as `createNew` returns), with no permission check.

On a handle whose row exists but can no longer be read (invalid JSON written later), every reading method (`getStatus`, `getParameters`, `getActivity`, `getPercentComplete`, `isCancelled`, `isVisibleTo`) throws `StructureRuntimeException`. For a row that no longer exists they return null, null, null, -1, false and false.

Stored values are read as follows: `C_STATUS` through `ProcessStatus.valueOf(int)` (any value other than 0 or 1 is FINISHED), `C_PERCENT_COMPLETE` null as -1, `C_CANCELLED` null as false, and JSON keys unknown to `ProcessDisplayParameters` or `I18nText` are ignored.

Process state is read through a cache per process ID (Jira cache `process-state`, entries expire 600 seconds after last access, property `structure.process.cache.timeout`). Every write made through this module (create, status, parameters, progress, cancel, delete) invalidates that ID, so the next read through any handle sees it; a change made to the table by other means is seen only after expiry or a cache clear. `clearCaches()` and both `clearUserCaches` variants drop the whole cache.

`setStatus(status)` on a handle stores `C_STATUS` and sets `C_TIMESTAMP` to the current time, even when the status is unchanged. A null status is ignored. If the row no longer exists, nothing is written and an error is logged.

`setParameters(params)` stores the parameters as JSON in `C_PARAMETERS` unless they are null or equal to the stored ones; it does not change `C_TIMESTAMP`. If the row no longer exists nothing is written.

`setProgress(activity, percent)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a percent below -1 or above 100, before anything is written. A null argument leaves that value unchanged (an activity, once set, cannot be cleared to null); a value equal to the stored one is not rewritten; if nothing is left to change, nothing is written. `C_TIMESTAMP` is not changed. -1 is accepted as "unknown".
`cancel()` sets `C_CANCELLED` to true if it is not yet true; the status is not changed and nothing is interrupted. Afterwards `isCancelled()` is true through every handle for that ID.

`isVisibleTo(user)` resolves the stored managing user key to a Jira user at call time. When the row has no managing user, and also when the stored key no longer belongs to any existing Jira user, the process is visible to everyone, including null (as the original does). Otherwise it is visible only to a user equal to the managing user.

`delete(id)` deletes the `AO_8BAD1B_PROCESS_STATE` row with that ID and invalidates its cache entry; afterwards the lookups return null and existing handles behave as for a missing row (writes are ignored with an error logged). Not determined: the effect of deleting an ID that has no row (passed to the Active Objects layer as is).

The user-key forms of `getInvisibleRows` and `collectInvisibleRows` treat a null key as the anonymous user; a non-null key is resolved with Jira's `UserManager.getUserByKey`, and when that returns null they throw `ForestAccessCache.UserLookupException` before checking anything.

`getInvisibleRows(rows, user)` returns an empty set for null or empty input. Otherwise it looks the rows up through `RowManager` and returns those (each once) whose item the user cannot see, judged through the item's type with the user's real permissions (no security override); rows that do not exist are included (and logged). A row whose item is a loop marker is judged by the item of the row the marker refers to.

Negative (temporary) row IDs passed to `getInvisibleRows`: with Java assertions enabled (as the tests run) the call throws `AssertionError`; with them disabled the negative IDs are dropped and only the others are checked (all negative gives an empty set).

Results of `getInvisibleRows` are cached per user: a row already checked for that user is answered from the cache without asking the item types again. When `ItemTracker` reports changed items, the cached results for the rows that show those items (found with `RowManager.findRows`) are dropped on that user's next call; a full update from the tracker drops the user's whole cache. All cached data is also dropped on the first call made more than 5 minutes after the last full clear.
